## Summary - add policy evidence for `gateway.nodes.allowCommands` and `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` entries - add `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` policy metadata and shape validation - report `policy/gateway-node-command-denied` when policy-denied node commands are not denied by OpenClaw config - document the new policy rule in the Policy CLI and plugin reference docs - classify `gateway.nodes.allowCommands.*` in policy config coverage  ## Policy syntax / evidence / finding contract  Policy syntax added by this PR:  ```jsonc {   "gateway": {     "nodes": {       "denyCommands": ["system.run"]     }   } } ```  `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` is an exact, case-sensitive deny-superset rule. An equal-or-stricter policy must include every command required by the baseline deny list. Empty or missing `denyCommands` means this rule is not active.  OpenClaw config evidence collected by policy doctor:  ```jsonc {   "gateway": {     "nodes": {       "allowCommands": ["mcp.help", "mcp.invoke", "system.run"],       "denyCommands": ["system.run"]     }   } } ```  The evidence scanner records concrete config entries as:  ```text kind=nodeAllowCommand command=system.run source=oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/allowCommands/#2 kind=nodeDenyCommand  command=system.run source=oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands/#0 ```  Finding emitted when policy requires a deny but config does not provide it:  ```json {   "checkId": "policy/gateway-node-command-denied",   "severity": "error",   "message": "Gateway node command 'system.run' is denied by policy but not denied by OpenClaw config.",   "path": "openclaw config",   "ocPath": "oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "target": "oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "requirement": "oc://policy.jsonc/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "fixHint": "Add 'system.run' to gateway.nodes.denyCommands or update policy after review." } ```  The finding clears when the config deny list contains the required exact command id. `allowCommands` evidence is collected for coverage and context; this PR only enforces the policy deny-superset contract.  ## Real behavior proof  Behavior or issue addressed: Managed policy can now require privileged gateway node commands such as `system.run` to be denied in OpenClaw config via `gateway.nodes.denyCommands`. The policy doctor reports the missing config deny and clears once the config denylist covers the policy denylist.  Real environment tested: Windows 11 PowerShell, `C:\src\openclaw-fork` checkout at PR head `cfe901e17963d9fe1833266a2758f125d7a51762`, source-harness invocation of the real policy doctor health checks through `runDoctorLintChecks`. Case `satisfied-config-deny`: wrote the same policy plus `openclaw.jsonc` with `gateway.nodes.denyCommands: ["system.run"]`.  Evidence after fix: ```text CASE missing-config-deny workspace: C:\Users\giodl\AppData\Local\Temp\oc-policy-missing-config-deny-Xk9xXX openclaw.jsonc gateway.nodes: {"allowCommands":["mcp.help","mcp.invoke","system.run"]} policy.jsonc gateway.nodes.denyCommands: ["system.run"] finding.checkId: policy/gateway-node-command-denied finding.severity: error finding.message: Gateway node command 'system.run' is denied by policy but not denied by OpenClaw config. finding.ocPath: oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands finding.target: oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands finding.requirement: oc://policy.jsonc/gateway/nodes/denyCommands finding.fixHint: Add 'system.run' to gateway.nodes.denyCommands or update policy after review. target.title: fix: media replies fail after prompt lock release
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users sending multiple visible message-tool media replies could see the embedded agent fail with `session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released` after the media had already been delivered.

The affected workflow is embedded agent delivery through channel message tools, especially batched image/media sends that mirror visible deliveries into the session transcript while the prompt lock is released.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prompt-lock recovery already preserves delivery mirror transcript appends, but the recovery classifier did not recognize side-append `leaf` controls written with those mirrors. This change treats only structurally valid `appendMode: "side"` leaf controls as prompt-released opaque entries so SessionManager can merge the delivery side branch, while active leaf controls remain takeover-triggering edits.

## User Impact

Users can receive batched media replies without the agent falsely reporting a session takeover during cleanup. The session takeover fence still rejects prompt-affecting branch changes and malformed leaf controls.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.session-lock.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 110 tests.
- `pnpm build` passed after adding the redacted prompt-release proof logs.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` passed with no accepted/actionable findings after the active-leaf guard was tightened.
- Live local proof on fixed gateway `2026.7.1-beta.1 (5c30bcf)`, 2026-07-05 02:14 Asia/Shanghai, redacted Weixin direct chat:
  - `message` tool started batched visible media sends at 02:14:20.
  - 11 local image uploads were attempted: 5 `hilton-*` images and 6 `yatu-*` images.
  - 11 `sendImageMessageWeixin: success` entries were logged between 02:14:21 and 02:14:27.
  - `prompt-released session change merged` was logged repeatedly during those media deliveries, showing prompt-released transcript changes were merged instead of treated as takeover.
  - `embedded run agent end ... isError=false` and `message processed ... outcome=completed` were logged at 02:14:30-02:14:31.
  - No new `session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released` or `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` entries appeared during the fixed-gateway test window; the only matching entries in the same local log were from the pre-fix npm-global run at 01:03.

target.title: fix(slack): preserve custom identity while streaming
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack agent replies posted with a configured display name/avatar lose that custom identity when draft or final preview updates use `chat.update`. Closes #58737. Supersedes the implementation in #93972 while preserving contributor credit for @MoerAI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Slack does not support `username`, `icon_url`, or `icon_emoji` on `chat.update`; the public method contract and current `@slack/web-api` type omit them, and the SDK maintainer confirms there is no update workaround. Slack now supports those authorship fields on `chat.startStream`.

This replacement therefore:

- forwards the configured identity through supported native stream starts;
- disables edit-based draft previews when a custom identity cannot use native streaming;
- delivers those replies once through the existing `chat.postMessage` path instead;
- converts deferred `missing_scope` stream-start failures into the existing post fallback so short replies are not lost.

## User Impact

Custom Slack agent names and avatars remain intact. Threaded/native-stream replies retain streaming UX; contexts that cannot use native streaming trade the edit preview for one correctly attributed final message.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/streaming.test.ts extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch.preview-fallback.test.ts` — 2 files, 106 tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox `tbx_01kwq9kbv377k5mhe81ghmsjja` — changed extension production/test typecheck, lint, guards, and import-cycle checks passed ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28717153797)).
- `pnpm build` and `pnpm check` passed during native prepare after rebase.
- Fresh structured autoreview accepted one deferred-start fallback finding; after the fix, the rerun reported no actionable findings.
- Official contracts checked: [`chat.update`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.update/), [`chat.startStream`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.startStream/), and [`@slack/web-api` request types](https://github.com/slackapi/node-slack-sdk/blob/f006ad409713741c5d398669c69ad98a7e090879/packages/web-api/src/types/request/chat.ts).

Known proof gap: a disposable live Slack canary was prepared but desktop 1Password authorization timed out; hosted exact-head CI remains required before merge.

target.title: fix(gateway,tui): queue-mode busy guard + queued-turn cancel contract
target.body:
Fixes #89059
Fixes #90012

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where TUI users sending a prompt during an active run would have the prompt blocked before Gateway queue handling could apply. It also fixes queued prompts becoming unabortable after the original `chat.send` client run finalized, which could let Esc or `/stop` report completion while queued work still executed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway and the auto-reply queue now own one queued-turn lifecycle across admission, collect-mode aggregation, transcript persistence, cancellation, dispatch, and terminal state. TUI remains a thin client: it forwards mid-run prompts, blocks only while admission is pending, and uses session-scoped abort for Esc and `/stop` even after a queued client run has left local UI state.

Queued cancellation remains requester-authorized by device or connection identity. Collect mode keeps cancellation owners in separate batches, retains queue-level cancellation after admission, and retires sibling client identities only when the aggregate has atomically acquired the reply lane.

## User Impact

TUI users can send follow-up and collect-mode prompts while an agent is running, intentionally repeat prompt text, cancel queued work reliably, and continue chatting after the queue drains. Failed post-admission bookkeeping no longer produces contradictory accepted-then-error terminal events, and queued transcript/media/context data stays attached to the collected turn.

target.title: fix(gateway): exit 0 on EADDRINUSE when healthy OpenClaw gateway is already running
target.body:
## Problem
When `openclaw gateway run` hits EADDRINUSE, it exits with code 1. Under systemd/launchd with `Restart=on-failure`, this creates a tight crash-loop.

## Root Cause
`GatewayLockError` on port conflict always exited non-zero, even when an already-healthy OpenClaw gateway was listening on that port.

## Fix
On EADDRINUSE, probe the gateway using the correct bind/TLS-aware URL with resolved auth credentials. Exit 0 only when a healthy OpenClaw instance is confirmed. Exit 1 for foreign processes or failed probes.

Probe handles all auth modes:
- **shared-secret** (token/password): forwarded directly
- **trusted-proxy**: synthetic proxy headers derived from config instead of shared-secret credentials
- **TLS with self-signed cert**: fingerprint loaded from `loadGatewayTlsRuntime` and pinned for the probe

Also fixes a pre-existing type error in `src/cli/update-cli.test.ts`.

Supersedes #29499 — thanks @BlueBirdBack for identifying the issue.

---

## AI-assisted

- [x] Built with Claude (Kees/OpenClaw) + Codex
- [x] Fully tested: VM gates (pnpm build + check + vitest gateway-cli + probe)
- [x] Author understands what the code does
- [x] Codex review findings addressed and resolved

target.title: fix(release): block stale Codex runtime pins
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The stable `@openclaw/codex` package could be published with an older embedded `@openai/codex` runtime even after a newer stable Codex release was available. Operators then saw the plugin as current because the updater correctly compared the published OpenClaw plugin version, while the route still launched the older runtime bundled by that package.

The canonical failure is release-time dependency freshness, not host CLI discovery or runtime binary attribution. On June 30, 2026, `@openclaw/codex@2026.6.11` was published with `@openai/codex@0.139.0` even though `@openai/codex@0.142.4` had already been published on June 29, 2026. The release pipeline validated internal package consistency but had no independent source of truth for whether the selected executable dependency was current.

Closes #99951.
Supersedes #99956 with the release-owner fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change keeps the invariant at the owner boundary:

- `@openclaw/codex` opts `@openai/codex` into a strict release-freshness contract through plugin metadata.
- The generic plugin release checker validates that each configured package is an exact runtime dependency.
- Release checks and release-plan collection resolve npm's `latest` dist-tag independently and fail closed when the pinned version is stale or cannot be verified.
- The check is opt-in, so ordinary plugin dependencies are not forced onto latest.

The Codex runtime is updated from `0.142.4` to `0.142.5`, generated lock data is refreshed, and the harness model snapshot is regenerated from the actual `0.142.5` app-server.

This deliberately does not add generic-core Codex version policy, inspect arbitrary selected binaries at runtime, or alter plugin update channel behavior. Those paths cannot prevent the stale artifact from being published and can report false positives for supported alternate routes.

## User Impact

Future Codex plugin releases cannot silently publish an older stable `@openai/codex` executable than npm's current `latest` release. A stale pin or unavailable freshness check blocks the release before users receive another false-green plugin update state.

The dependency bump also moves the next published Codex plugin runtime to `0.142.5`.

## Evidence

Behavior addressed: Prevent stale Codex executable pins from passing OpenClaw plugin release validation.

Real environment tested: macOS source checkout with the installed `@openai/codex@0.142.5` app-server, plus an AWS Linux Crabbox `c7a.8xlarge` changed-lane run.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/plugin-npm-release.test.ts test/plugin-clawhub-release.test.ts test/scripts/release-wrapper-scripts.test.ts extensions/codex/src/manifest.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/models.test.ts`
- `node scripts/generate-npm-shrinkwrap.mjs --package-dir extensions/codex --check`
- `node --import tsx scripts/plugin-npm-release-check.ts --plugins @openclaw/codex`
- `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --provider aws --label codex-release-dependency-freshness --timing-json -- env OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 corepack pnpm check:changed`
- `$autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output`

Evidence after fix:

- 5 focused test files passed across 3 Vitest shards, 76 tests total.
- The Codex shrinkwrap check and live npm-backed plugin release check passed.
- Crabbox run `run_871522b80992` passed the changed gate, including dependency/shrinkwrap guards, full typecheck, lint, and import-cycle checks.
- Fresh Codex autoreview returned no actionable findings (`patch is correct`, confidence `0.83`).
- A real `codex app-server` `model/list` probe reported server version `0.142.5`; the documented public model snapshot was updated from that response.

Observed result after fix: A configured executable dependency below npm `latest`, or a registry failure that prevents verification, rejects plugin release planning instead of accepting a self-consistent stale artifact.

What was not tested: Publishing to npm was not performed. Existing installed `@openclaw/codex@2026.6.11` packages remain unchanged until a new plugin release is published and installed.

target.title: fix: propagate gateway TLS fingerprints to bootstrap clients
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Gateway clients bootstrapped outside `callGateway` (ACP, MCP channel bridge, and native approval handling) did not receive the local TLS certificate fingerprint for a self-signed local WSS gateway.
- Why it matters: those clients could fail TLS verification even when the local gateway bootstrap had enough information to trust the generated certificate.
- What changed: added a shared TLS fingerprint resolver, reused it from `callGateway`, propagated `bootstrap.tlsFingerprint` into ACP/MCP/approval `GatewayClient` construction, and added regression coverage for local, remote, override, and non-TLS cases.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no gateway server TLS behavior, auth mode, config schema, environment variable, or public endpoint changed.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening

target.title: fix: suggest checking auth for bundled providers in model-not-found error (fixes #100066)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a bundled provider (e.g. `anthropic`, `openai`, `microsoft-foundry`) has no authenticated profile, requesting one of its models produces an error message that tells operators to add a `models.providers[]` config entry. Following that advice causes the config validator to reject the config (if the provider id isn't recognized as bundled) or produces a no-op overlay (if it is). Either way, the operator is stuck in a loop: the runtime says "add config" → the validator says "that's wrong" → the gateway crash-loops.

This contradictory guidance was reported in issue #100066 where an operator using `openai-codex` followed the error message verbatim and ended up with a gateway that wouldn't boot.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bundled providers are registered automatically at startup — they don't need `models.providers[]` config entries. When a model from a bundled provider is missing, the most likely cause is a missing or expired auth profile, not a missing config entry.

The fix adds a check using `isBuiltInModelProviderOverlayId()` before generating the error message. For bundled providers, the message now suggests running `openclaw models status` to check provider auth. For non-bundled (custom) providers, the existing config-entry guidance is preserved.

## User Impact

Operators who encounter model-not-found errors for bundled providers will now get actionable guidance pointing to the actual cause (missing auth) instead of misleading config instructions that crash the gateway.

## Changes Made

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.ts`: Import `isBuiltInModelProviderOverlayId`, add bundled-provider check in `buildMissingProviderModelRegistrationHint` before the config-entry fallback
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts`: Update existing test for bundled provider error message, add new test for non-bundled provider error message

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed:** Error message guidance when a bundled provider model is not found in the registry
- **Environment tested:** macOS, Node 22.22.3, OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (local checkout at 7a0188c)
- **Steps run after the patch:** Invoked `resolveModelAsync` for bundled provider `anthropic` and non-bundled provider `custom-provider` with models referenced in `agents.defaults.models` but no provider config
- **Evidence after fix:**
```
$ npx tsx test-bundled-provider-error.mjs
ERROR: Unknown model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5. Found agents.defaults.models["anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5"], but the bundled provider "anthropic" has no registered model "claude-sonnet-4-5". This usually means the provider has no authenticated profile — run `openclaw models status` to check provider auth and re-authenticate if needed. See https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/model-providers.

$ npx tsx test-custom-provider-error.mjs
ERROR: Unknown model: custom-provider/some-model. Found agents.defaults.models["custom-provider/some-model"], but no matching models.providers["custom-provider"].models[] entry. Add { "id": "some-model", "name": "some-model" } to models.providers["custom-provider"].models[] to register this provider model. For custom or proxy providers, also set api and baseUrl so requests route to the intended endpoint. See https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/model-providers.
```
- **Observed result after fix:** Bundled providers now show auth-check guidance; non-bundled providers retain the config-entry guidance
- **What was not tested:** End-to-end gateway startup with a bundled provider lacking auth (requires full gateway orchestration)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Error message guidance for bundled vs non-bundled provider model-not-found
- **Environment tested:** macOS, Node 22.22.3, OpenClaw 2026.6.11 local checkout
- **Steps run after the patch:** Called `resolveModelAsync` (the production model resolution entry point) for bundled provider `anthropic` and non-bundled provider `custom-provider`
- **Evidence after fix:**
```
Bundled provider (anthropic):
ERROR: Unknown model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5. Found agents.defaults.models["anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5"], but the bundled provider "anthropic" has no registered model "claude-sonnet-4-5". This usually means the provider has no authenticated profile — run `openclaw models status` to check provider auth and re-authenticate if needed. See https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/model-providers.

Non-bundled provider (custom-provider):
ERROR: Unknown model: custom-provider/some-model. Found agents.defaults.models["custom-provider/some-model"], but no matching models.providers["custom-provider"].models[] entry. Add { "id": "some-model", "name": "some-model" } to models.providers["custom-provider"].models[] to register this provider model. For custom or proxy providers, also set api and baseUrl so requests route to the intended endpoint. See https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/model-providers.
```
- **Observed result after fix:** Bundled providers show auth guidance; non-bundled providers show config guidance
- **What was not tested:** Full gateway startup scenario with bundled provider lacking auth

target.title: test(infra): make Windows-render and late-SQLite guard tests pass on macOS hosts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #100025. Two infra tests fail deterministically on any pristine macOS checkout of `main` (Linux CI green on the same SHA), which breaks the `scripts/pr prepare-run` local `pnpm test` gate on maintainer Macs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both failures are test-environment assumptions, not product bugs:

- `src/infra/exec-approvals-analysis.test.ts` resolves the real host `python3`; Homebrew's `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/python@3.14/.../bin/python3.14` contains `@`, so the enforced-command renderer correctly quotes the executable, and the assertion regex rejected the closing quote. The regex now allows an optional `"` before the script argument.
- `src/infra/backup-create.test.ts` injects a late SQLite file from an `fs.readdir` spy keyed on `path.resolve(state.stateDir)`. Snapshot discovery scans the realpathed dir, and on macOS the tmpdir-based state dir goes through the `/var -> /private/var` symlink, so the spy never fired and the guard had nothing to catch. The spy now also compares against `fs.realpath(state.stateDir)`.

## User Impact

None at runtime (test-only). Maintainers can land PRs from macOS again: `pnpm test` infra shard goes green on a clean checkout of `main`.

## Evidence

On macOS (Darwin 25.5), pristine clone of `main`, before: 3 failed (2 late-SQLite variants + Windows-render). After:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-analysis.test.ts src/infra/backup-create.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  59 passed (59)
```

Linux behavior is unchanged (`/tmp` is not a symlink; `/usr/bin/python3` needs no quoting) — CI on this PR is the Linux proof.

target.title: feat(xai): add realtime voice provider
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw Talk already has a realtime provider contract and gateway-relay path, but the bundled xAI plugin did not expose Grok Voice Agent as a native realtime voice provider.

Without this, users who want xAI/Grok voice in OpenClaw either cannot use it through Talk or have to fall back to a lower-quality STT -> model -> TTS loop. That is especially limiting for long-running assistants where supplier choice and realtime voice cost matter.

Closes #99087.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one canonical bundled xAI realtime voice provider through the existing Talk `gateway-relay` contract instead of creating a separate voice stack.

The provider:

- connects to xAI realtime voice (`grok-voice-latest`) over WebSocket;
- registers through the existing `registerRealtimeVoiceProvider` seam;
- exposes the provider through the xAI plugin manifest;
- maps audio, transcript, tool-call, cancellation, and close events into the existing Talk realtime bridge contract;
- keeps secrets out of docs and evidence.

The follow-up commits also address the ClawSweeper/Codex review findings: interrupted assistant audio is now paired with `response.cancel` plus `conversation.item.truncate`, the relay playback race preserves the assistant item until truncation is possible, and assistant transcript deltas are buffered so delta-only xAI completion still emits a final transcript.

Dependency note: `ws` is intentionally moved into the xAI runtime dependency set because the new provider imports it at runtime. The repository dependency guard correctly requires maintainer/security approval for the exact head SHA or a maintainer-owned regeneration path. This PR does not try to bypass that policy.

## User Impact

Users selecting xAI realtime Talk get native Grok voice replies through the existing OpenClaw Talk relay path rather than a synthetic STT/TTS loop.

Expected behavior:

- Talk can select `provider: "xai"` with `transport: "gateway-relay"`.
- Gateway-relay clients can stream mic audio and receive Grok voice audio.
- Barge-in cancels the active response and truncates only the currently interrupted assistant audio.
- Completed assistant audio and previous-turn assistant items are not truncated on later turns.

This is intentionally scoped to the xAI realtime voice provider and Talk relay integration. It does not weaken gateway auth and does not include secrets or production token values.

## What Problem This Solves

Portable agent tool-result construction was duplicated across multiple plugins. Exact pretty-JSON result builders repeatedly recreated the same contract: one text block containing `JSON.stringify(payload, null, 2)` plus the same typed payload in `details`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a narrow `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results` entrypoint that exposes the canonical typed `textResult` and `jsonResult` helpers, then migrates only callers with identical contracts. MCP structured/error results, browser sanitization, media/file results, approvals, channel presentation, transport envelopes, and caller-specific failure semantics remain with their existing owners.

The consolidation removes local constructors and one duplicate result type while preserving the existing model-facing text and structured details behavior.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Plugin tools keep returning the same text and `details` payloads. Plugin authors gain a small supported SDK seam for portable text and pretty-JSON agent results.

### SDK surface metric and merge risk

- Public entrypoints: **+1** (`323 -> 324`)
- Public exports: **+3** (`10,425 -> 10,428`)
- Public callable exports: **+2** (`5,237 -> 5,239`)

This is an additive public SDK contract, so the matching package export, API metadata/checksum, docs, and exact surface-budget ceilings are updated together. target.title: fix(daemon): refuse duplicate launchd gateway managers
target.body:
Closes #97178

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running the gateway under a system-domain LaunchDaemon could later run `openclaw gateway install` from a user session and silently add a duplicate gui-domain LaunchAgent for the same gateway label and port. That duplicate manager setup can restart-loop the gateway and disconnect clients.

## Why This Change Was Made

The macOS launchd installer now checks for a same-label system LaunchDaemon before it writes or bootstraps the user LaunchAgent. If `launchctl print system/<label>` succeeds or a matching `/Library/LaunchDaemons/<label>.plist` exists, install refuses with recovery guidance instead of creating a second KeepAlive manager. This intentionally stays narrow and does not add full system LaunchDaemon install/stop/uninstall lifecycle support.

AI-assisted: yes. I understand the change: it adds a pre-write launchd conflict guard and focused mocked launchd regressions for the reported duplicate-manager path.

## User Impact

Headless macOS operators who already manage the gateway as a system LaunchDaemon get a clear stop-and-fix error instead of a second user LaunchAgent that can fight the system daemon on the same port.

## Evidence

Behavior addressed: `openclaw gateway install` refuses to write/bootstrap a gui-domain LaunchAgent when a same-label system LaunchDaemon is loaded or present on disk.

Real environment tested: local source checkout with mocked launchd states; the issue reporter supplied live headless macOS LaunchDaemon evidence on #97178. I did not mutate a real system LaunchDaemon on this host.

Exact steps:

```shell
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/launchd.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/launchd.test.ts src/daemon/inspect.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/status.gather.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Evidence after fix: the new launchd tests cover both `launchctl print system/ai.openclaw.gateway` reporting a loaded daemon and `/Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist` existing when the system job is not printed.

Observed result: focused launchd test passed; the broader daemon/status proof set passed in 2 Vitest shards.

What was not tested: live install against a disposable headless macOS host with a real system LaunchDaemon, to avoid creating or disturbing host-level launchd services from this automation run.


---

**Runtime proof — captured before/after (negative-control harness, macOS, Node 22):**

Exercised end-to-end through the real `installLaunchAgent` → `writeLaunchAgentPlist` → `assertNoSystemLaunchDaemonConflict` → real `execFile` path; only the external `launchctl` binary is mocked (a PATH shim), plist writes go to a scratch `HOME`. Same harness ran on unfixed `main` and on this branch.

_Before — unfixed `main` (negative control):_

```
Scenario A (no conflict, proceeds)  : PASS
Scenario B (conflict, refuses)      : FAIL
>>> UNFIXED: with a same-label system LaunchDaemon present, install did NOT
    refuse and WROTE the gui LaunchAgent plist anyway.  (the #97178 bug)
```

_After — this branch:_

```
Scenario A (no conflict, proceeds)  : PASS
Scenario B (conflict, refuses)      : PASS
error (verbatim): Existing system LaunchDaemon system/ai.openclaw.gateway detected at
  /Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist. Refusing to install a gui-domain
  LaunchAgent for the same gateway label because duplicate launchd managers can
  restart-loop the gateway. ... sudo launchctl bootout system/ai.openclaw.gateway ...
plist written : false
>>> FIXED: the guard refused the duplicate manager with recovery guidance.
```

**What was not tested:** a live install against a disposable macOS host with a real system LaunchDaemon over a live port; and the on-disk `/Library/LaunchDaemons/<label>.plist` branch (needs a root-owned path via `sudo touch`/`rm`) — it shares the same throw site as the proven `launchctl print` branch.


---

**Branch-(b) proof — REAL root-owned `/Library/LaunchDaemons` plist (addresses the "mock-backed proof" review note):**

Re-ran on macOS with a genuine root-owned `/Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist` (`sudo touch`), and with `launchctl print system/<label>` forced to report NOT-loaded (exit 113) so the **only** conflict signal is the real on-disk system plist — the `launchctl` shim plays no part in the decision. This exercises the real `/Library/LaunchDaemons` filesystem check (`LAUNCH_DAEMON_SYSTEM_DIR`) end-to-end.

_PR branch (`9f0f82df78`) — exit 0:_

```
launchctl print system/<label> : NOT-loaded (113)  -> branch-(a) inert
real /Library/LaunchDaemons plist present : yes     -> branch-(b) is the signal
install threw  : true
error (verbatim):
  | Existing system LaunchDaemon system/ai.openclaw.gateway detected at /Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist.
  | Refusing to install a gui-domain LaunchAgent for the same gateway label because duplicate launchd managers can restart-loop the gateway.
  | Keep the system LaunchDaemon, or remove it first with `sudo launchctl bootout system/ai.openclaw.gateway` and `sudo rm /Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist`, then rerun `openclaw gateway install`.
gui LaunchAgent written : false
>>> FIXED: install refused via the REAL root-owned system plist (branch-b).
```

_`main` (`29f5e9d35c`, no guard) — exit 1, negative control:_

```
launchctl print system/<label> : NOT-loaded (113)   real plist present : yes
install threw  : false
gui LaunchAgent written : true
>>> UNFIXED: install IGNORED the real system plist and wrote the gui LaunchAgent anyway — the #97178 bug.
```

target.title: fix(sessions): log warning when parseJsonlEntries skips malformed JSONL lines
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three JSONL reader functions in session-manager.ts silently skip malformed transcript lines with bare catch blocks and zero diagnostic output. When a transcript file is corrupted, entries vanish with no operator visibility — no log, no warning, no metric.

This adds counted malformed-line detection and a single `logWarn` summary to all three readers: `parseJsonlEntries` (session load), `buildSessionInfo` (session listing), and `parseSessionEntries` (CLI history, BTW continuation, fork-source, embedded file state).

## Why This Change Was Made

Data loss without observability is the worst failure mode. The write side was hardened (`serializeJsonLine` throws on non-serializable roots), but transcripts already on disk from older code remain vulnerable. This adds the reader-side visibility so operators can detect and act on corruption.

## Evidence

### Committed test proof

Three test cases cover the warning behavior:

- `parseSessionEntries > logs a warning and skips malformed JSONL lines while preserving valid entries`
- `parseSessionEntries > reports the correct skip count for multiple malformed lines`
- `parseSessionEntries > parseJsonlEntries logs warning for malformed lines via loadEntriesFromFile`

### Local test run — 53/53 passed

```
pnpm test src/agents/sessions/session-manager.test.ts
```

## Risk

target.title: refactor: consolidate byte-size formatting
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw had ten independent byte-size scaling and unit-selection implementations across core, Control UI, agent-core, QQBot, and file-transfer surfaces. Their binary thresholds, SI/IEC labels, precision, spacing, and rounding rules were implicit in local loops, making compatible output changes difficult to review and easy to drift.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one dependency-free `normalization-core` formatter whose call sites explicitly select `si`, `iec`, or `legacy-binary` style together with precision, spacing, maximum unit, and floor rounding where required. Owner wrappers retain invalid-input and presentation policy, plugin callers use the existing `plugin-sdk/number-runtime` entrypoint, and the distinct rounded-MiB promotion contract in `src/infra/disk-space.ts` remains local.

The exact production TypeScript numstat is `+127/-83` (net `+44`), calculated file-by-file with new files included and tests excluded. The positive LOC is intentional: ten separate scaling/unit-selection algorithms become one 45-line canonical implementation, while explicit style options preserve user-visible compatibility and prevent hidden SI/IEC label drift. Narrowing the migration would keep duplicate algorithms without removing the canonical owner.

Maintained packages such as `pretty-bytes` and `filesize` were considered, but `normalization-core` is intentionally dependency-free and these callers require exact legacy labels plus per-unit precision and rounding contracts.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible output changes. Existing byte labels, precision, spacing, unit caps, invalid-value fallbacks, and threshold behavior remain compatible. Plugin and core developers now have one focused formatter contract instead of copying another local loop.

## Evidence

- Focused compatibility matrix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/normalization-core/src/format.test.ts src/commands/doctor-disk-space.test.ts packages/agent-core/src/harness/utils/truncate.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/agents-utils.test.ts ui/src/ui/controllers/skill-workshop.test.ts ui/src/ui/control-ui-vite-config.node.test.ts src/agents/tool-images.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.test.ts extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/params.test.ts` — passed 7 Vitest shards.

Closes #99977

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Linux gateway port diagnostics could report the wrong listener process when the requested port is a prefix of another listener port, such as inspecting 1878 while ss output contains 127.0.0.1:18789.

AI-assisted. I understand the change: it keeps the Linux ss fallback parser on the existing port-diagnostics path, but changes its listener row match from substring search to exact parsed TCP endpoint port equality.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Linux ss parser was the only listener parser in this module still selecting the local address column with a substring match. This reuses the existing parseTcpEndpoint helper, matching the sibling netstat parser behavior without changing lsof, Windows, process enrichment, or probe fallback behavior.

## User Impact

Operators running OpenClaw gateway diagnostics on Linux get more reliable process ownership reports and are less likely to stop an unrelated process when troubleshooting a busy gateway port.

target.title: fix: WebChat stop fails for WeChat channel sessions
target.body:
Related: #91987

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes WebChat `/stop` failing to stop looping channel-originated agent turns, observed with a WeChat channel session selected in WebChat.

## Why This Change Was Made

WebChat exact stop text now bypasses slash-menu selection and is submitted as the typed command, so `/stop` reliably reaches the abort path.

The gateway abort path now preserves the selected explicit channel session key across the active state used by this flow:

- `chatAbortControllers` for normal WebChat/chat runs
- hidden registered or pre-registered channel runs when the request names that explicit channel session
- `replyRunRegistry` for active channel auto-reply operations that do not have a chat abort controller

Broad `agent:main`/global stop requests no longer infer a hidden channel session. They abort only matching visible/global scope unless the request already carries the explicit channel session key.

## User Impact

Users viewing a WeChat/channel session in WebChat can stop a looping channel agent with `/stop`. Broad visible sessions still do not accidentally stop unrelated hidden channel work.

## Evidence

Video proof:

- Before fix:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1107f4e1-8450-4f2b-981a-ac5815673ed2

- After fix, selected WeChat channel session `/stop` stops the channel loop:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25f32135-1f1a-4f9c-b0a7-ddade5464b86

- After fix, main session `/stop` does not affect the running WeChat channel session:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/969c19dd-bec6-42a4-a39f-3e526c58e045

- **Multi-channel isolation proof:** after fix, WeChat and Telegram channel sessions are both running at the same time; WebChat has the WeChat channel session selected; sending `/stop` aborts only the selected WeChat channel run, while the Telegram channel run continues unaffected. This video is the explicit proof for the multi-channel stop-isolation case.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5b78d13-90c5-416f-a354-610fef9b6c59

Redacted terminal/log proof from a local PR-head build:

- The second block is WebChat with the main session selected while the WeChat channel run is still active. The UI sends `chat.abort` for `agent:main:main`; Gateway returns `aborted=false runIds=[]`, and the same WeChat run continues afterward.

target.title: fix(memory-core): treat dreaming fence marker lines as inside-fence in promotion guard (#80613)
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem.** `lineRangeOverlapsDreamingFence` in `extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.ts` tracked `insideFence` state from the fence marker lines but never flagged ranges that included the marker lines themselves. A relocated promotion range that ended on a `<!-- openclaw:dreaming:*:start -->` line, began on a `<!-- openclaw:dreaming:*:end -->` line, or covered only a marker line passed the guard, and the snippet built from those raw lines carried the marker text into `MEMORY.md`.
- **Why it matters.** The guard's contract is to refuse rehydrated ranges that overlap managed dreaming fences so dream artifacts cannot be promoted. Treating the marker lines themselves as outside-the-fence leaves a narrow but real leak: any window the relocator picks that clips a marker produces a snippet that includes the literal `<!-- openclaw:dreaming:*:start/end -->` text, and (when the window straddles content on either side of the marker) the adjacent line. This is the residual edge case noted by ClawSweeper on #80702 ("the managed-block leak half is related but should be handled by a focused memory-core promotion fix"), narrowed to the guard itself rather than a parallel sanitizer.
- **What changed.** `extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.ts`: marker lines are now checked against the range bounds; if a marker is inside the relocated range, the range is rejected. The pre-existing inside-fence tracking remains so interior lines between a start/end pair are still flagged. The contract elsewhere — the contamination predicate, the relocator, the apply path, the `MEMORY.md` writer — is untouched.
- **What did not change (scope boundary).** No change to `relocateCandidateRange`, `isContaminatedDreamingSnippet`, `applyShortTermPromotions`, `buildDailySnippetChunks`, `stripManagedDailyDreamingLines`, the CJK dedupe path (the second sub-bug of #80613 is being addressed separately by #80620), or any `MEMORY.md` rendering. No new sanitizer is introduced — this is a narrowing of the existing guard.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Refs #80613 (does not fully close; the dramatic full-Candidate leak from the issue body is already prevented by the merged fence-overlap guard in #68774. This PR narrows a residual marker-line edge case in the same guard.)
- Related: #80620 (CJK dedupe half, separate PR), #80702 (closed sanitizer approach, intentionally not duplicated here).
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior addressed: `lineRangeOverlapsDreamingFence` now flags relocated promotion ranges that include a dreaming fence marker line, preventing the marker text (and any adjacent fenced content captured by the same raw-line window) from being promoted into `MEMORY.md`.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS (Apple Silicon, Node v22.14.0, pnpm 11.1.0). The fix is mechanical and exercised by Vitest unit tests against the helper directly.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  - `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.test.ts -t "lineRangeOverlapsDreamingFence"` — targeted run of the affected describe block.
  - `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.test.ts` — full file regression.
  - `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.test.ts` — adjacent file regression.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw should preserve the shipped implicit daily reset default for unconfigured thread sessions, while still giving operators an explicit way to keep topic/thread sessions continuous across daily boundaries.

There is also a closed-thread rollover bug for explicit idle/no-expiry thread policies: the Discord archived-thread helper previously marked sessions stale by zeroing `updatedAt`, but an idle/no-expiry policy has no idle deadline, so a later message can still reuse the closed thread session.

## Fix

- Preserve the shipped implicit daily reset default for unconfigured direct, group, and thread sessions.
- Document explicit topic/thread continuity with `session.resetByType.thread: { mode: "idle", idleMinutes: 0 }`.
- Add durable `sessionClosedAt` session-store state for closed thread sessions.
- Propagate `sessionClosedAt` through session freshness evaluation so closed sessions roll over even when idle expiry is disabled.

target.title: feat(agents): enforce computer-use policy in Claude CLI runtime
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Claude CLI sessions could receive OpenClaw-managed MCP servers, including computer-use, but the generic CLI path could not enforce OpenClaw's effective per-tool policy before native Claude MCP calls reached the upstream server. This made direct computer-use integration incomplete and left Claude's own permission settings as a separate enforcement surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change promotes the existing `claude-stdio` transport into a persistent runtime-like path while keeping `claude-cli` correctly modeled as a `CliBackend`. OpenClaw-managed external MCP servers are routed through an OpenClaw-owned proxy that filters discovery, applies the effective global/provider/agent/group/sender/sandbox policy, relays pre/post tool hooks, preserves native backend-owned MCP entries, and supports stdio, HTTP/SSE, and WebSocket upstreams.

The reserved Claude server name `computer-use` is rewritten only in the generated launch config. OpenClaw policy continues to use the configured server identity, and Claude's native computer-use namespace is explicitly disabled so calls cannot bypass the managed proxy.

## User Impact

Operators can use an OpenClaw-managed computer-use MCP server with `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"` and a narrow `toolFilter`. Claude sees only allowed tools, every forwarded operation is authorized by OpenClaw first, and follow-up turns retain the same sender/auth context and live runtime session.

Native backend `--mcp-config` entries remain Claude-owned and byte-preserved unless an OpenClaw-managed server intentionally replaces the same identity.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(watch-node): defer restart when dist/entry.js is missing mid-rebuild
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: When a git pull triggers source file changes while `dist/` is mid-rebuild, the hot-reload watcher (`watch-node.mjs`) kills the current healthy gateway process and restarts into a missing `dist/entry.js`, causing an 8x crash-loop that exhausts systemd's restart limit.

**Solution**: Check build readiness before restarting. The new `isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs)` function verifies that both `dist/entry.js` exists AND the build stamp's git HEAD matches the current checkout HEAD. If either check fails (missing entry, mismatched HEAD, missing stamp, or stamp without HEAD), the restart is deferred and polled every 2s until the build is verified fresh. An additional guard in the child-process exit handler prevents crash-looping when the watcher would otherwise restart into a stale build after a child exit.

**Review response – P1 fix**: The background rebuild now passes `OPENCLAW_SKIP_OUTPUT_CLEAN=1`, which causes `tsdown-build.mjs` to skip `cleanTsdownOutputRoots()` at its entrypoint — preventing dist/ cleanup under the live gateway.

**What changed**: Three files — `scripts/watch-node.mjs`, `scripts/tsdown-build.mjs`, and `test/scripts/watch-node.test.ts`.

**What did NOT change**: Build logic, source watch paths, the `dist/` IGNORE segment, or `run-node.mjs`.

Fixes #99603

## What Problem This Solves

Production gateway deployments using a git checkout with hot-reload (via systemd) are vulnerable to a crash-loop when a `git pull` triggers a rebuild while `dist/` is mid-build. The watcher kills the currently-healthy gateway and restarts into a missing entrypoint. This caused a 37-minute production outage on 2026-07-03.

## Root Cause

`watch-node.mjs:requestRestart()` unconditionally sends SIGTERM to the healthy gateway child process whenever chokidar detects a relevant source file change (e.g. from `git pull`). During a rebuild, `tsdown-build.mjs` calls `cleanTsdownOutputRoots()` which removes `dist/entry.js`. The new child then crashes because the entrypoint doesn't exist, and `shouldRestartAfterChildExit()` treats SIGTERM/exit code 143 as restartable — forming a crash-loop.

**Additionally**: Even when an old `dist/entry.js` exists, the current git HEAD may have changed (after `git pull`), meaning `run-node` will rebuild and clean `dist` after the stop. The old entrypoint check alone is insufficient to prevent the crash-loop.

## Changes

`scripts/watch-node.mjs` (+97 / -37 lines):

### Layer 1 — `isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs, resolveHead)`

Replaces the previous `isDistEntryFresh()` mtime check with a comprehensive build-readiness check:
- Verifies `dist/entry.js` exists (basic guard for mid-rebuild window)
- Reads the `.buildstamp` file from `dist/` and compares its recorded `head` against the current checkout HEAD via `resolveGitHead()`
- If HEADs differ, or if the stamp lacks a `head` but the current HEAD is known, the build is stale — restart is deferred
- Falls back gracefully (entry-only check) when git or stamp file is unavailable

### Layer 2 — Deferred polling (existing, retained)

When build is not ready, polls every 2s instead of dropping the restart request. When the build completes (entry.js + matching stamp appear), auto-triggers the restart.

### Layer 3 — Exit handler guard

On child-process exit (SIGTERM/143), verifies build readiness before restarting. Prevents self-reinforcing crash-loop when the child exits during a rebuild window.

### Layer 4 — Background rebuild without dist/ cleanup (review response)

`triggerBackgroundRebuild()` spawns `tsdown-build.mjs` to rebuild in the background while the current gateway stays alive. The spawn now passes `OPENCLAW_SKIP_OUTPUT_CLEAN=1` in the child environment, which causes the tsdown-build wrapper to skip `cleanTsdownOutputRoots()` at its entrypoint.

After the rebuild exits successfully, only the build stamp is written. The runtime postbuild stamp is intentionally NOT written here — updating it without syncing runtime artifacts would create a false positive for run-node on next start.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: The hot-reload watcher no longer kills the current healthy gateway child process when the build output is missing or stale for the current checkout. The background rebuild no longer cleans dist/ under the live gateway (P1 review fix).

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v24.1.0 — L2 evidence via code analysis (env var guard verification) against the worktree git checkout. 20/20 unit tests pass.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```terminal
❯ pnpm test -- test/scripts/watch-node.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
   Duration  2.08s

❯ node -e "const fs = require('fs'); const src = fs.readFileSync('scripts/tsdown-build.mjs','utf8'); console.log(src.includes('OPENCLAW_SKIP_OUTPUT_CLEAN') ? 'P1 guard present ✅' : 'P1 guard MISSING ❌')"
P1 guard present ✅
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```js
// tsdown-build.mjs entrypoint — clean is skipped when env var is set
if (process.env.OPENCLAW_SKIP_OUTPUT_CLEAN !== "1") {
    cleanTsdownOutputRoots();
}
```

The guard prevents `cleanTsdownOutputRoots()` from running during background rebuild, which is spawned by `triggerBackgroundRebuild()` with `OPENCLAW_SKIP_OUTPUT_CLEAN=1`:

```js
// watch-node.mjs — background rebuild spawn
rebuildChildProcess = deps.spawn(deps.process.execPath, compilerArgs, {
    cwd: deps.cwd,
    env: { ...childEnv, OPENCLAW_SKIP_OUTPUT_CLEAN: "1" },
    stdio: ["inherit", "pipe", "pipe"],
});
```

20/20 tests pass covering: build readiness matching, stamp edge cases, deferred restart polling, exit handler guard, background rebuild lifecycle, and stamp consistency.

**Observed result after the fix**: P1 — the background rebuild no longer cleans `dist/` while the live gateway is still serving. The `tsdown-build.mjs` wrapper skips `cleanTsdownOutputRoots()` when `OPENCLAW_SKIP_OUTPUT_CLEAN=1` is set. The runtime postbuild stamp is not written from the background rebuild context; run-node resolves runtime postbuild on next cold start.

**What was not tested**: Full gateway integration with live `gateway:watch` + `git pull` to reproduce the exact systemd restart race. This requires a controlled environment with systemd-managed gateway and concurrent git operations. The L2 coverage (code analysis + 20 passing tests) verifies all code paths.

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low risk — change is constrained to `triggerBackgroundRebuild()` guard logic and exit handler; no impact on build, runtime, or non-watch paths
- [x] All behaviors are additive (env var check + stamp write); when env var is absent, behavior is identical to current code
- [x] 20 tests added/updated covering all code paths
- [x] No config, API, or dependency changes
- [x] Does not affect production (non-watch) gateway usage

## Review

- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes

target.title: [codex] Keep ambiguous delivery attempts recoverable
target.body:
## Summary

- Keeps outbound delivery entries in ambiguous post-send states pending when adapter reconciliation is unavailable.
- Preserves the existing no-blind-replay behavior while leaving the entry retryable for later reconciliation/backoff.
- Avoids consuming retry budget when no reconciliation-capable adapter ran, so ambiguous entries do not age into terminal failure before a later adapter can reconcile them.
- Treats a reconciliation-capable adapter returning `null` as a completed unresolved reconciliation attempt, so that path still consumes retry budget and respects the max-retry cap.
- Updates startup recovery, reconnect-drain, and outbound queue integration coverage plus Discord troubleshooting guidance for #87544.

## Scope

This is a narrow mitigation for #87544 and intentionally does not close the full issue. The broader transcript-to-provider delivery ledger, Discord reconciliation semantics, and UI/API surfacing still need maintainer design.

## Validation

- Automation main refresh (2026-07-05 JST): merged `openclaw/openclaw@614e87cce1d4fcfd0bdfe1a622f95006c0ab7ce9` into the PR branch; resolved conflicts in the outbound recovery/storage tests and helpers; pushed head `a3b4c97865598e78c6b5f0c5057af508982758ed`.
- GitHub pre-refresh state checked: PR had become `CONFLICTING` / `DIRTY` after main advanced. Prior lightweight checks and Real behavior proof were passing before the refresh, and `gh pr checks --required` reported no required checks on the branch.
- Review threads checked with GraphQL: 4 total, 0 unresolved; current-head storage-thread reply remains resolved. Existing connector reviews are `COMMENTED` only and are not treated as approval.
- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/docs-list.js`
- `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check`
- `corepack pnpm format:check src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts docs/channels/troubleshooting.md`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`
  - 4 files passed across 2 Vitest shards, 68 tests passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main`
  - Clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: ambiguous outbound delivery entries whose platform send may have started must not be blindly replayed, and must remain pending/recoverable without consuming retry budget when adapter reconciliation is unavailable.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS with Node v22.22.3, rebased onto `openclaw/openclaw@c5d34c8376f8aa32744786cae0473c60e39ef444`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran a one-off `node --import tsx --input-type=module` terminal proof that invoked the real `enqueueDelivery`, `markDeliveryPlatformOutcomeUnknown`, `recoverPendingDeliveries`, `loadPendingDeliveries`, and SQLite state reader against a temporary OpenClaw state directory. The proof queued an `unknown_after_send` outbound entry, ran recovery with no reconciliation-capable adapter, and failed if `deliver` was called, the entry did not remain pending, or retry budget was consumed.

Evidence after fix:

```text
info: Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
warn: Delivery entry <redacted-queue-id> delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation
warn: Retry failed for delivery <redacted-queue-id>: delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation
info: Delivery recovery complete: 0 recovered, 1 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
proof summary: {"recovered":0,"failed":1,"skippedMaxRetries":0,"deferredBackoff":0}
deliver call count: 0
pending entries: 1
queue row: {"status":"pending","retry_count":0,"recovery_state":"unknown_after_send","last_error":"delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation"}
```

Observed result after fix: recovery refused blind replay, did not call the delivery function, kept exactly one pending queue entry, and persisted `status: "pending"`, `retry_count: 0`, and `recovery_state: "unknown_after_send"`.

What was not tested: no live Discord gateway/channel send was performed in this pass. The broader transcript-to-provider delivery ledger, Discord reconciliation semantics, and Control UI/API delivery-state surface remain open under #87544.

## Root cause
The cron setup watchdog emits 'cron: isolated agent setup timed out before runner start' when an isolated agent run stalls before the runner starts, but the retry classifier on origin/main does not recognize the sibling phrasing 'isolated agent setup stalled before runner start' as retryable.

## Fix
Broadened the timeout classifier through a named TIMEOUT_PATTERN so setup/pre-execution watchdog prose is treated as timeout while leaving the scheduler, watchdog, and restart paths unchanged.

## Test
Updated src/cron/retry-hint.test.ts to assert setup/pre-execution watchdog failures classify as retryable timeout errors.

## Sibling occurrences
Grepped src/cron for related timeout/setup watchdog wording; the only uncovered sibling was 'isolated agent setup stalled before runner start', now covered.

Portable agent tool-result construction was duplicated across multiple plugins. Exact pretty-JSON result builders repeatedly recreated the same contract: one text block containing `JSON.stringify(payload, null, 2)` plus the same typed payload in `details`.

target.title: refactor: extract reusable AI runtime package
target.body:
Closes #99040

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's model protocol adapters and streaming registry were embedded in the main application, so other packages could not reuse the proven Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Google, Vertex, Mistral, and ChatGPT/Codex transports without taking on OpenClaw's application runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extracts one public package: `@openclaw/ai`. It contains the provider-neutral model/message/tool contracts, validation, diagnostics, event streams, isolated runtime registry, and lazy provider adapters. `packages/llm-core` remains a private implementation package and is bundled into `@openclaw/ai`; consumers never install or publish a second OpenClaw AI package.

The package is genuinely self-contained. Pure transport helpers that previously lived in application code (tool projections and strict-schema normalization, system-prompt cache boundary, stream first-event timeout, streaming byte guard, deferred event buffer, Anthropic model contract/refusal/auth-header helpers, OpenAI reasoning-effort and responses-stream compat, reasoning-tag text partitioner, LLM request activity) moved into `packages/ai`; `utf16-slice` moved into `@openclaw/normalization-core`. Host policy stays in OpenClaw and is injected through a narrow `AiTransportHost` port (`configureAiTransportHost`): guarded model fetch (SSRF policy), secret redaction for tool-result replay, OpenAI strict-tool defaults, and diagnostics logging. Library defaults are inert; `src/llm/stream.ts` installs OpenClaw's implementations. There are no relative imports from the package back into `src/`.

The public barrel is instance-first: `createApiRegistry()` / `createLlmRuntime()` plus contracts and the host port. The process-default registry/runtime and their bound helpers moved behind `@openclaw/ai/internal/*`, which exists for OpenClaw itself and carries no semver guarantee (documented in the README). `registerBuiltInApiProviders(registry)` takes an explicit registry. Built-in provider registration is table-driven, replacing ~420 lines of per-provider boilerplate.

OpenClaw consumes `@openclaw/ai` as a normal workspace dependency, which `pnpm pack` converts to the exact release version. Runtime stream construction resolves through `@openclaw/ai/event-stream`, preserving one `EventStream` constructor identity across OpenClaw, agent-core, and external consumers. The release workflow packs, verifies, and publishes `@openclaw/ai` before the root package, and `packages/ai` now ships its own `npm-shrinkwrap.json` so its transitive dependency tree stays pinned at user install time even though workspace deps are omitted from the root shrinkwrap.

## User Impact

Existing OpenClaw users should see no configuration, model selection, authentication, or streaming behavior change. Installing `openclaw` installs the exact `@openclaw/ai` release automatically, with the AI package's dependency tree pinned by its own shrinkwrap. Library consumers can depend on the one package, create isolated runtimes, and opt into the eight built-in API adapters without inheriting a mutable process-global registry.

## Evidence

- `pnpm build` passed end to end: package declarations, root bundle, CLI/bootstrap guards, runtime postbuild, plugin SDK export check, and Control UI build.
- `pnpm tsgo` and `pnpm check:test-types` pass; the `tsdown.config.ts` `dts.neverBundle` option was moved to its correct `deps.dts` home (the previous placement was a type error that broke `check-test-types` on CI).
- The `checks-node-compact-*` CI failures (`Cannot find module @openclaw/ai/dist/providers.mjs`) were root-caused to three Node-side alias tables that only knew `@openclaw/llm-core`: `src/plugin-sdk/root-alias.cjs`, `src/plugins/plugin-sdk-native-resolver.ts`, and `src/plugins/sdk-alias.ts`. All now cover the `@openclaw/ai` export map (and the new `normalization-core/utf16-slice` subpath); the previously failing tests (`models-config.applies-config-env-vars`, `model-selection`) pass locally.
- `check-dependencies` (knip) is clean: `packages/ai` declares only its six real runtime deps (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google/Mistral SDKs, partial-json, typebox); orphaned root deps (`@mistralai/mistralai`, `partial-json`) removed; knip config knows the new package's entry points.
- Focused suites pass locally via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`: all of `packages/ai`, `src/llm`, `packages/agent-core`, `packages/normalization-core`, transport streams, model selection/config, custom API registry, and the host-port integration proofs (SSRF fetch-proof, redaction contract, OpenAI-compatible auth) — 869 tests, 0 failures.
- `pnpm check:changed` run over the full branch diff.
- Fresh Codex autoreview completed clean with no accepted/actionable findings.
- `examples/ai-chat` is a minimal external-consumer app that uses only the public package surface against the built dist (isolated runtime + built-in provider registration + one streamed completion). Live-verified end to end against a local Ollama server through the OpenAI-completions transport: streamed text deltas, `stop=stop`, token usage reported.

target.title: fix(agent-core): resolve tool-name mismatches for Claude Code alias calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents trained on Claude Code emit tool names such as `KnowledgeSearch`, `Glob`, and `Grep`. These names don't exist in a stock OpenClaw runtime, producing `Tool X not found` errors and causing the model to retry the same call until it gives up.

LCM corpus analysis on a private deployment (2026-03-15 – 2026-07-01):

| Tool name called | Failures |
|---|---|
| KnowledgeSearch | 2,586 |
| Glob | 1,234 |
| Grep | 159 |
| **Total covered by this PR** | **3,979 across ~1,400 conversations** |
| Agent (not covered — see below) | 429 |

Representative failure trace (redacted):
```
tool_call   toolCallId=[redacted]  toolName=Glob  arguments={"pattern":"[redacted]"}
tool_result toolCallId=[redacted]  toolName=Glob  isError=true
            content=[{"type":"text","text":"Tool Glob not found"}]
```
The model retried twice more with the same tool name, got the same error, and gave up.

## Fix

Add `resolveToolAlias()` before the deferred-tool resolver in `resolveToolCallTool()`:

1. **Case-insensitive exact match** — catches capitalisation drift (e.g. `READ` → `Read`).
2. **Normalised alias map** — strips non-alphanumeric characters, then tries ordered fallback names:
   - `KnowledgeSearch` → `memory_search`, `knowledge_search`, `wiki_search`, `search`
   - `Glob` → `find`
   - `Grep` → `grep`

The alias table is intentionally scoped to tools with **argument-compatible schemas** — a single query/pattern string. That's why `Agent`/`Task` are **not** in this PR: Claude Code emits `Agent(prompt="...")` but `sessions_spawn` takes `task`, and rewriting arguments belongs in the deployment's own tool catalog (where full schema context lives), not in a shared alias table. Deployments that want the Agent alias can bind it themselves with the correct arg translation — this PR gets 92% of the failure class right without coupling the resolver to any one tool's schema.

The deferred-tool resolver path is also alias-aware: when `resolveDeferredTool()` materialises a tool under its canonical name (e.g. `memory_search`) for an alias call (e.g. `KnowledgeSearch`), the dispatcher now accepts that as a valid resolution instead of throwing on the name mismatch — while still rejecting resolvers that return genuinely unrelated names.

When no alias matches, the not-found error now lists the agent's available tool names, which helps both the model self-correct and operators diagnose missing tool registrations.

The original tool-call name is preserved in the trajectory and tool-result audit identity so sessions are replay-identical to the pre-fix behaviour, except the call succeeds instead of erroring. Replay is deterministic because alias resolution is a pure function of the requested name and the agent's tool context.

## Tests

Six tests in the deferred-tool hydration suite (`agent-loop.test.ts`), 22/22 passing:

- `KnowledgeSearch` dispatches to `memory_search` (alias case).
- Case-insensitive lookup (`FIND` → `find`).
- Not-found error includes available tool list.
- `Agent` with a `sessions_spawn` tool present still returns not-found (regression against premature Agent alias).
- Deferred-tool resolver returning an alias-equivalent name (`memory_search` for `KnowledgeSearch`) is accepted and dispatched.
- Deferred-tool resolver returning an unrelated name (`not_related` for `KnowledgeSearch`) is still rejected.

Local: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts` → 22 passed.

## Evidence

**Before (pre-patch):** 3,979 `Tool * not found` failures across the three aliases covered by this PR (LCM analysis, full corpus 2026-03-15 – 2026-07-01) — see the table above. An additional 429 Agent failures are documented but intentionally out of scope for the reasons stated in the Fix section.

**After (post-patch):** the fix has been running as a local dist patch on a private OpenClaw deployment since 2026-07-02T14:43 (updated 2026-07-02T23:45Z to match this PR's head, including canonical dispatch identity). The `promptAppend` mitigation that previously steered models toward native tool names — flagged in the last review as suppressing organic alias calls — was **removed** at 2026-07-02T23:45Z and the gateway restarted, restoring natural model behaviour.

### Post-fix positive trace (2026-07-03)

~1 hour after the mitigation was lifted, the embedded memory-search subagent organically emitted a Claude Code alias call in a real production turn, and it dispatched through the resolver (redacted; source is the deployment's lossless message store — embedded subagents persist no session `.jsonl`, so tool calls are recorded there as message parts):

```
conversation: active-memory-[redacted]   (embedded memory-search subagent, live fleet traffic)

2026-07-03T00:46:07Z  assistant  tool_use     toolCallId=toolu_01Pn[redacted]
                                 toolName=KnowledgeSearch
                                 arguments={"query":"[redacted]"}
2026-07-03T00:46:07Z  tool       tool_result  toolCallId=toolu_01Pn[redacted]
                                 toolName=memory_search   isError=false
                                 content={"results":[{"path":"[redacted]","startLine":15,
                                 "endLine":18,"score":0.96,"snippet":"[redacted]",
                                 "source":"memory","corpus":"memory"}, …]}
```

Two properties, both matching this PR's documented behaviour:

1. **The alias call dispatched to the canonical tool and returned real results.** Pre-patch, the identical call shape produced `Tool KnowledgeSearch not found` and model retries (see the corpus above; last such failures 2026-07-01, 12 that day).

target.title: fix(watch-node): defer restart when dist/entry.js is missing mid-rebuild
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: When a git pull triggers source file changes while `dist/` is mid-rebuild, the hot-reload watcher (`watch-node.mjs`) kills the current healthy gateway process and restarts into a missing `dist/entry.js`, causing an 8x crash-loop that exhausts systemd's restart limit.

**Solution**: Check build readiness before restarting. The new `isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs)` function verifies that both `dist/entry.js` exists AND the build stamp's git HEAD matches the current checkout HEAD. If either check fails (missing entry, mismatched HEAD, missing stamp, or stamp without HEAD), the restart is deferred and polled every 2s until the build is verified fresh. An additional guard in the child-process exit handler prevents crash-looping when the watcher would otherwise restart into a stale build after a child exit.

**Review response – P1 fix**: The background rebuild now passes `OPENCLAW_SKIP_OUTPUT_CLEAN=1`, which causes `tsdown-build.mjs` to skip `cleanTsdownOutputRoots()` at its entrypoint — preventing dist/ cleanup under the live gateway.

**What changed**: Three files — `scripts/watch-node.mjs`, `scripts/tsdown-build.mjs`, and `test/scripts/watch-node.test.ts`.

**What did NOT change**: Build logic, source watch paths, the `dist/` IGNORE segment, or `run-node.mjs`.

Fixes #99603

## What Problem This Solves

Production gateway deployments using a git checkout with hot-reload (via systemd) are vulnerable to a crash-loop when a `git pull` triggers a rebuild while `dist/` is mid-build. The watcher kills the currently-healthy gateway and restarts into a missing entrypoint. This caused a 37-minute production outage on 2026-07-03.

## Root Cause

`watch-node.mjs:requestRestart()` unconditionally sends SIGTERM to the healthy gateway child process whenever chokidar detects a relevant source file change (e.g. from `git pull`). During a rebuild, `tsdown-build.mjs` calls `cleanTsdownOutputRoots()` which removes `dist/entry.js`. The new child then crashes because the entrypoint doesn't exist, and `shouldRestartAfterChildExit()` treats SIGTERM/exit code 143 as restartable — forming a crash-loop.

**Additionally**: Even when an old `dist/entry.js` exists, the current git HEAD may have changed (after `git pull`), meaning `run-node` will rebuild and clean `dist` after the stop. The old entrypoint check alone is insufficient to prevent the crash-loop.

## Changes

`scripts/watch-node.mjs` (+97 / -37 lines):

### Layer 1 — `isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs, resolveHead)`

Replaces the previous `isDistEntryFresh()` mtime check with a comprehensive build-readiness check:
- Verifies `dist/entry.js` exists (basic guard for mid-rebuild window)
- Reads the `.buildstamp` file from `dist/` and compares its recorded `head` against the current checkout HEAD via `resolveGitHead()`
- If HEADs differ, or if the stamp lacks a `head` but the current HEAD is known, the build is stale — restart is deferred
- Falls back gracefully (entry-only check) when git or stamp file is unavailable

### Layer 2 — Deferred polling (existing, retained)

When build is not ready, polls every 2s instead of dropping the restart request. When the build completes (entry.js + matching stamp appear), auto-triggers the restart.

### Layer 3 — Exit handler guard

On child-process exit (SIGTERM/143), verifies build readiness before restarting. Prevents self-reinforcing crash-loop when the child exits during a rebuild window.

### Layer 4 — Background rebuild without dist/ cleanup (review response)

`triggerBackgroundRebuild()` spawns `tsdown-build.mjs` to rebuild in the background while the current gateway stays alive. The spawn now passes `OPENCLAW_SKIP_OUTPUT_CLEAN=1` in the child environment, which causes the tsdown-build wrapper to skip `cleanTsdownOutputRoots()` at its entrypoint.

After the rebuild exits successfully, only the build stamp is written. The runtime postbuild stamp is intentionally NOT written here — updating it without syncing runtime artifacts would create a false positive for run-node on next start.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: The hot-reload watcher no longer kills the current healthy gateway child process when the build output is missing or stale for the current checkout. The background rebuild no longer cleans dist/ under the live gateway (P1 review fix).

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v24.1.0 — L2 evidence via code analysis (env var guard verification) against the worktree git checkout. 20/20 unit tests pass.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```terminal
❯ pnpm test -- test/scripts/watch-node.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
   Duration  2.08s

❯ node -e "const fs = require('fs'); const src = fs.readFileSync('scripts/tsdown-build.mjs','utf8'); console.log(src.includes('OPENCLAW_SKIP_OUTPUT_CLEAN') ? 'P1 guard present ✅' : 'P1 guard MISSING ❌')"
P1 guard present ✅
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```js
// tsdown-build.mjs entrypoint — clean is skipped when env var is set
if (process.env.OPENCLAW_SKIP_OUTPUT_CLEAN !== "1") {
    cleanTsdownOutputRoots();
}
```

The guard prevents `cleanTsdownOutputRoots()` from running during background rebuild, which is spawned by `triggerBackgroundRebuild()` with `OPENCLAW_SKIP_OUTPUT_CLEAN=1`:

```js
// watch-node.mjs — background rebuild spawn
rebuildChildProcess = deps.spawn(deps.process.execPath, compilerArgs, {
    cwd: deps.cwd,
    env: { ...childEnv, OPENCLAW_SKIP_OUTPUT_CLEAN: "1" },
    stdio: ["inherit", "pipe", "pipe"],
});
```

20/20 tests pass covering: build readiness matching, stamp edge cases, deferred restart polling, exit handler guard, background rebuild lifecycle, and stamp consistency.

**Observed result after the fix**: P1 — the background rebuild no longer cleans `dist/` while the live gateway is still serving. The `tsdown-build.mjs` wrapper skips `cleanTsdownOutputRoots()` when `OPENCLAW_SKIP_OUTPUT_CLEAN=1` is set. The runtime postbuild stamp is not written from the background rebuild context; run-node resolves runtime postbuild on next cold start.

**What was not tested**: Full gateway integration with live `gateway:watch` + `git pull` to reproduce the exact systemd restart race. This requires a controlled environment with systemd-managed gateway and concurrent git operations. The L2 coverage (code analysis + 20 passing tests) verifies all code paths.

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low risk — change is constrained to `triggerBackgroundRebuild()` guard logic and exit handler; no impact on build, runtime, or non-watch paths
- [x] All behaviors are additive (env var check + stamp write); when env var is absent, behavior is identical to current code
- [x] 20 tests added/updated covering all code paths
- [x] No config, API, or dependency changes
- [x] Does not affect production (non-watch) gateway usage

## Review

- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes
