target.title: fix(cron): retry isolated setup watchdog stalls
target.body:
## Summary

Fix cron retry classification for isolated-agent setup watchdog failures that stall before the runner starts.

## Root cause

Cron's retry policy is driven by `resolveCronExecutionRetryHint`, which classifies an error message against configured transient categories. The setup watchdog path can fail with prose like:

- `cron: isolated agent setup stalled before runner start`

That message is a transient setup timeout, but it did not contain the existing timeout tokens (`timeout`, `timed out`, `stalled before execution start`, `ETIMEDOUT`). As a result, cron jobs configured with `retryOn: ["timeout"]` did not treat this pre-runner setup stall as retryable, so Pablo task execution cron failures could stop instead of retrying.

## Fix

- Extracted the timeout regex into `TIMEOUT_PATTERN` for readability.
- Added the isolated setup watchdog text to timeout matching.
- Added regression coverage that verifies setup/pre-execution watchdog messages classify as `timeout` retries.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts src/cron/retry-hint.test.ts` passed: 1 file, 6 tests.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.

Known local gate issues while validating:

- The requested command `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/cron/retry-hint.test.ts` exits with "No test files found" because `vitest.unit.config.ts` excludes `src/cron/**`; the cron shard command above is the matching config for this test.
- `pnpm format:check` currently reports existing formatting differences across many unrelated files.
- `pnpm lint` currently fails in the plugin-sdk boundary root shims generation step with `rolldown-plugin-dts` errors while building existing plugin SDK `.d.ts` entries; no lint finding points at the cron retry files.

target.body:
## Summary

Adds the first real implementation slice for #82017: `sessions_spawn` now accepts an optional execution placement request and validates it against `agents.executionBackends`.

This PR keeps runtime behavior conservative: the built-in `local` `process` backend is the only executable backend in this release. Forward-looking `container` and `kubernetes` configs are accepted by config validation, but spawn rejects them with an explicit runtime-policy error until those backends are implemented. Placement is recorded on spawned run metadata/list output for readback; non-local runner dispatch is intentionally not implemented here.

## Related PRs

- Runtime self-context / runtime tool companion: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90101

## CONTRIBUTING alignment

- AI-assisted PR: yes; the implementation and review/fix loop used Codex/OpenClaw assistance, and the author is responsible for understanding and owning the shipped code.
- Current-head real behavior proof: included below for `ae6a3f7fdfb1`, covering default local process placement, configured local profile placement, and unsupported Kubernetes fail-closed behavior.
- Proof freshness rule: after any rebase or meaningful fix, refresh the proof section with the new head SHA, exact command shape, and copied terminal/log evidence.
- Bot review status: ClawSweeper has marked contributor proof sufficient and ready for maintainer look; the remaining action is maintainer approval of the public contract.
- Takeover readiness: maintainer edits are enabled, related PR #90101 is linked, and this PR intentionally does not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Maintainer contract decision requested

Please explicitly choose one before merge:

- Approve the v1 additive contract: `agents.executionBackends` plus `sessions_spawn.execution`, with only local `process` execution implemented in this slice and `container`/`kubernetes` configs accepted but rejected fail-closed at spawn time.
- Narrow before merge: restrict the schema/docs to local `process` only until non-local backend semantics are fully designed.
- Pause for broader design: hold this PR until runtime self-context, execution placement, and remote worker protocol decisions are reviewed together.

## Linked issue

Related to #82017.

## What changed

- Added `agents.executionBackends` config schema/types/help/labels/tags/docs.
- Added `sessions_spawn.execution.backend/profile` schema and plumbing.
- Added placement resolution for subagent and ACP spawns.
- Persisted execution placement into subagent run records and list output.
- Regenerated prompt snapshots for the new model-facing tool schema.
- Added unit coverage for config validation, placement resolution, tool parameter forwarding, and list readback.

## Behavior

- Omitted execution request defaults to `{ backend: "local", type: "process" }`.
- Configured local process profiles can be requested by name, validated, and recorded on the run.
- Unknown backends/profiles fail before spawn starts.
- `container`/`kubernetes` backends are schema-valid but rejected at spawn time for now.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: `sessions_spawn.execution` placement resolution accepts the default local process backend, accepts a configured local profile, and rejects an unsupported Kubernetes backend instead of silently falling back.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw repository checkout at branch `feat/execution-backends-local`, rebased on `origin/main`, running the patched TypeScript source with Node/tsx.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```sh
node --import tsx <<'EOF'
import { resolveAgentExecutionPlacement } from './src/agents/execution-backends.ts';

const cfg = {
  agents: {
    executionBackends: {
      local: {
        type: 'process',
        profiles: {
          small: { resources: { requests: { cpu: '500m', memory: '1Gi' } } },
        },
      },
      k8s: {
        type: 'kubernetes',
        profiles: { 'large-build': {} },
      },
    },
  },
};

for (const [name, request] of [
  ['default local process', undefined],
  ['local small profile', { backend: 'local', profile: 'small' }],
  ['unsupported k8s backend', { backend: 'k8s', profile: 'large-build' }],
]) {
  console.log(`${name}: ${JSON.stringify(resolveAgentExecutionPlacement({ cfg, request }))}`);
}
EOF
```

- Evidence after fix (copied live terminal output):

```text
default local process: {"ok":true,"execution":{"backend":"local","type":"process"}}
local small profile: {"ok":true,"execution":{"backend":"local","type":"process","profile":"small"}}
unsupported k8s backend: {"ok":false,"error":"execution backend \"k8s\" has type \"kubernetes\", but only local process execution is supported in this release"}
```

- Observed result after fix: local process placement resolves successfully, the configured `small` profile is preserved in the placement result, and unsupported Kubernetes placement returns an explicit runtime-policy error.

target.title: feat(clickclack): publish durable agent activity rows (commentary + tool)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `extensions/clickclack` channel extension only delivered the final prose reply, so a ClickClack channel showed nothing while an agent turn ran, even though the ClickClack server natively stores and renders durable `agent_commentary` / `agent_tool` message rows (with `turn_id` grouping and a dedicated non-inherited `agent_activity:write` bot scope). This PR adds an opt-in activity publisher to the extension: when an account sets `agentActivity: true` and its bot token carries `agent_activity:write`, streamed commentary and tool progress from the in-process `replyOptions.onItemEvent` seam are POSTed as durable activity rows (and PATCHed as snapshots grow), coalesced so one logical step becomes one row. Tool rows render through the shared `buildChannelProgressDraftLine` formatter, so ClickClack shows the same tool name + command detail as the Discord/Slack/Telegram progress lines. Publishing is best-effort: transport failures are logged and never interrupt final text delivery, and the flag defaults to off so stock setups and older ClickClack servers are untouched.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

**Behavior:** With a ClickClack account bound to an agent, sending a channel message runs the agent turn invisibly: no commentary, no tool activity, only the final reply. After this PR (with `agentActivity: true` and a bot token carrying `agent_activity:write`), durable commentary and tool rows stream into the channel while the turn runs.

**Real environment:** Real gateway built from this repo (`pnpm build`, `node openclaw.mjs gateway`), real ClickClack server built from upstream `clickclack` source at `main@51a375d` (`go build ./apps/api/cmd/clickclack`, sqlite, dev bootstrap), real model turns (`anthropic/claude-opus-4-6`) with exec tools, stock ClickClack web UI in Chromium driven through the composer. BEFORE gateway is built at the merge base `bd2740fedc`; AFTER gateway is built at this PR head. Same server instance, same channel name, same steps.

**Exact steps:**
1. Run the ClickClack server (`clickclack serve`, dev bootstrap) and create an empty `#agent-demo` channel.
2. Configure `channels.clickclack` with `baseUrl`, a bot token, `replyMode: "agent"`; BEFORE uses the merge-base build (no `agentActivity` key exists there), AFTER uses this PR's build with `agentActivity: true` and a bot token that carries `agent_activity:write`.
3. Start the gateway, open `#agent-demo` in the ClickClack web UI, and type into the composer: "Check what OS version this server is running, how much free disk space it has, and how many files are in your workspace directory. Narrate what you are doing between steps, then give me a two-line summary."
4. Watch the channel while the turn runs, then open the reply thread.

**Evidence (before):** https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/clickclack-before-prose-only.gif (frame-by-frame contact sheet: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/before-final_sheet.png)

**Evidence (after):** https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/clickclack-after-agent-activity.gif (frame-by-frame contact sheet: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/after-final_sheet.png)

**Observed result:** BEFORE: the channel stays empty for the whole turn; a lone "1 reply" thread chip appears at the end and the thread contains only the final summary. AFTER: one `agent_commentary` row ("Checking OS version, disk space, and workspace file count all at once…") and three `agent_tool` rows ("🛠️ show /etc/os-release …", "🛠️ df -h /", "🛠️ find files in … -> run wc") stream into the channel during the turn, grouped by `turn_id`, and the final summary lands in the thread as before. Stored rows verified over the ClickClack REST API (`kind: agent_commentary` / `agent_tool`, shared `turn_id`).

**What was not tested:** DM conversations (the publisher targets `direct_conversation_id`, covered by unit tests, but the live capture is a channel); multi-account setups beyond one account; a ClickClack server predating the activity kinds (degradation there relies on the opt-in default staying off plus best-effort error logging, exercised in unit tests, not live); non-embedded (CLI-backend) agent runtimes.

### Clean-room validation
- Command: fresh clone of `pull/99954/head` (`82bc62ed46`) inside a stock `node:22-bookworm` container: `git fetch --depth 1 origin pull/99954/head && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm vitest run extensions/clickclack`
- Provider / lease: plain Docker container (crabbox delegated providers unavailable on this host: `blacksmith` and `sbx` binaries not installed, no AWS credentials — stated per proof policy rather than skipped silently)
- Result: **34/34 tests passed, 6/6 files** on the fresh clone

### Tests, build, lint
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/clickclack` — 6 files, 32 tests passed (includes 7 new activity-publisher tests + new accounts/http-client/inbound cases)
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — exit 0
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — exit 0
- `pnpm oxlint extensions/clickclack` — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `pnpm config:channels:check` — bundled channel-config metadata in sync (regenerated in this PR for the new `agentActivity` key)
- `pnpm build` — full build passes; the AFTER evidence runs this exact build

## Findings
None open. Two defects were caught and fixed during my own validation pass before posting: (1) the generated bundled channel-config metadata initially wasn't regenerated, which made gateway startup reject `agentActivity` as an unknown key; (2) item events are gated on tool-summary visibility, so the publisher declares channel-owned progress rendering (`suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages: true`) to receive events regardless of session verbose mode, matching the draft-compositor precedent.

## Lineage
None. Consumes the existing `replyOptions.onItemEvent` / `commentaryProgressEnabled` seam already used by the Discord/Telegram/Slack draft paths. The ClickClack server side (activity kinds, `turn_id`, `agent_activity:write` scope) is already merged upstream in the ClickClack repo.

## Remaining risk
Low. The feature is off by default and fully additive; with the flag off the extension behavior is byte-identical to before. With the flag on, publisher failures are logged best-effort and cannot break final delivery (single promise chain isolates transport errors). The main thing to watch is row volume on long multi-tool turns: one row per tool call plus one per commentary segment, PATCH-coalesced within a 700ms debounce window.

- Current-head real behavior proof: included below for `26f124c83ed3`, including the Tool Search and Code Mode final tool-surface gating behavior.
- Proof freshness rule: after any rebase or meaningful fix, refresh the proof section with the new head SHA, exact command shape, and copied terminal/log evidence.
- Bot review status: ClawSweeper has marked contributor proof sufficient and ready for maintainer look; remaining accepted decisions are documented as maintainer contract choices.
- Takeover readiness: maintainer edits are enabled, related PR #84758 is linked, and this PR intentionally does not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Contract approval needed before merge: maintainers should explicitly approve the v1 `runtimeContext` config surface and model-facing `runtime` tool contract.

## Goal

Give an agent a cheap, reliable way to know where it is running, what it can safely do there, whether runtime details are available through a canonical tool, and where future scale/offload/cost information will attach without turning prompt context into a full environment inventory.

Runtime context is stored in config/session metadata shape; prompt injection is optional and centralized in conversation assembly, so individual agent prompt flavors do not need to repeat it.

## Implemented v1 slice

- Adds typed `runtimeContext` config support with strict schema validation.
- Supports exposure modes: `none`, `tool_hint`, and `prompt_summary`.
- Injects runtime self-context through the existing hidden `openclaw.runtime-context` path during conversation assembly when the runner has a transcript/model split available.
- Keeps `none` fully silent: no prompt injection and no runtime tool.
- Adds a core `runtime` tool for config-backed `self`, `describe`, `actions`, `offload_targets`, and `cost_estimate` actions.
- Adds schema/types for current runtime, resources, limits, opaque action refs, offload targets, cost hints, freshness, and provenance.
- Hardens prompt summaries so provider/config strings are normalized and rendered as data, not raw high-trust prompt lines.
- Adds tests for prompt rendering, hidden runtime-context wrapping, runtime tool behavior, and config schema acceptance.
- Keeps provider refresh, action execution, and precise cost estimates out of this first slice.

## Team review findings addressed

- Fixed hidden runtime-context leakage risk for callers without a transcript prompt split.
- Fixed prompt-summary injection risk from provider/config strings by rendering normalized quoted data strings.
- Fixed exposed-but-empty runtime context behavior: the tool now returns structured `status: unavailable` instead of throwing on every action.
- Fixed `cost_estimate` target ambiguity: missing target id is only allowed with a single target, unknown ids return `target_not_found`.
- Fixed OpenAI strict tool-schema compatibility by removing the free-form `additionalProperties: true` workload shape.
- Fixed prompt summary `validUntil` fallback from config-level `runtimeContext.validUntil`.

## Non-goals

- No broad environment inventory in v1.
- No scheduler/load model.
- No capacity slots.
- No CPU/memory class fields.
- No raw provider commands in prompt-facing data.
- No provider-backed runtime refresh yet.
- No action-ref execution yet.
- No precise provider cost estimator yet.

target.title: Keep legacy WhatsApp crontab lint opt-in
target.body:
## Summary
- mark `core/doctor/legacy-whatsapp-crontab` default-disabled so default `doctor --lint` does not invoke the shell-backed `crontab -l` probe
- preserve explicit selection through `--only core/doctor/legacy-whatsapp-crontab` and `--all`
- keep the ordered Doctor legacy-cron contribution wired through the existing `healthCheckIds` mapping instead of duplicating core checks inline

## Public surface
- No public SDK/plugin/config contract changes.
- Default `doctor --lint` changes only by skipping this live crontab probe; `--all` and `--only` still include it.
- Real repair/reporting behavior for the legacy WhatsApp crontab path remains owned by the existing Doctor implementation.

## PR surface
- 2 files changed, +45/-2 after removing the duplicate inline contribution checks and preserving the existing core check mapping.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Default `doctor --lint` leaves the legacy WhatsApp crontab probe opt-in, while explicit `--only core/doctor/legacy-whatsapp-crontab` still runs the detector and reports the warning.

Real environment tested:
WSL Ubuntu source checkout at head `8964ccb23931a3c0d8e09122f4dff6cfbbd960b4`; built OpenClaw doctor lint CLI module from this checkout; isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; PATH-scoped temporary `crontab` shim returning a redacted legacy `~/.openclaw/bin/ensure-whatsapp.sh` entry. The real system crontab was not modified.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. `pnpm build`
2. `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<tmp> PATH=<tmp>:$PATH runDoctorLintCli({json:true})`
3. `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<tmp> PATH=<tmp>:$PATH runDoctorLintCli({json:true, onlyIds:["core/doctor/legacy-whatsapp-crontab"]})`

Evidence after fix:
```json
{
  "defaultRun": {
    "exitCode": 1,
    "checksRun": 23,
    "checksSkipped": 23,
    "findingCount": 31,
    "crontabShimCalls": "<none>",
    "hasLegacyWhatsAppCrontabFinding": false
  },
  "explicitOnlyRun": {
    "exitCode": 1,
    "checksRun": 1,
    "checksSkipped": 45,
    "findingCount": 1,
    "crontabShimCalls": "called: -l",
    "legacyWhatsAppCrontabFindings": [
      {
        "checkId": "core/doctor/legacy-whatsapp-crontab",
        "severity": "warning",
        "message": "Legacy WhatsApp crontab health check detected.",
        "fixHint": "`~/.openclaw/bin/ensure-whatsapp.sh` is not maintained by current OpenClaw and can misreport `Gateway inactive` from cron when the systemd user bus environment is missing.\nRemove the stale crontab entry with crontab -e; use openclaw channels status --probe, openclaw doctor, and openclaw gateway status for current health checks.\nMatched 1 entry."
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Observed result after fix:
Default lint did not call `crontab -l` and did not include `core/doctor/legacy-whatsapp-crontab`. Explicit `--only core/doctor/legacy-whatsapp-crontab` called `crontab -l` once and emitted the structured warning finding.

What was not tested:
A real user crontab was not edited; the crontab content was supplied by a PATH-scoped shim to avoid mutating host cron state. target.title: feat(clickclack): publish durable agent activity rows (commentary + tool)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `extensions/clickclack` channel extension only delivered the final prose reply, so a ClickClack channel showed nothing while an agent turn ran, even though the ClickClack server natively stores and renders durable `agent_commentary` / `agent_tool` message rows (with `turn_id` grouping and a dedicated non-inherited `agent_activity:write` bot scope). This PR adds an opt-in activity publisher to the extension: when an account sets `agentActivity: true` and its bot token carries `agent_activity:write`, streamed commentary and tool progress from the in-process `replyOptions.onItemEvent` seam are POSTed as durable activity rows (and PATCHed as snapshots grow), coalesced so one logical step becomes one row. Tool rows render through the shared `buildChannelProgressDraftLine` formatter, so ClickClack shows the same tool name + command detail as the Discord/Slack/Telegram progress lines. Publishing is best-effort: transport failures are logged and never interrupt final text delivery, and the flag defaults to off so stock setups and older ClickClack servers are untouched.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

**Behavior:** With a ClickClack account bound to an agent, sending a channel message runs the agent turn invisibly: no commentary, no tool activity, only the final reply. After this PR (with `agentActivity: true` and a bot token carrying `agent_activity:write`), durable commentary and tool rows stream into the channel while the turn runs.

**Real environment:** Real gateway built from this repo (`pnpm build`, `node openclaw.mjs gateway`), real ClickClack server built from upstream `clickclack` source at `main@51a375d` (`go build ./apps/api/cmd/clickclack`, sqlite, dev bootstrap), real model turns (`anthropic/claude-opus-4-6`) with exec tools, stock ClickClack web UI in Chromium driven through the composer. BEFORE gateway is built at the merge base `bd2740fedc`; AFTER gateway is built at this PR head. Same server instance, same channel name, same steps.

**Exact steps:**
1. Run the ClickClack server (`clickclack serve`, dev bootstrap) and create an empty `#agent-demo` channel.
2. Configure `channels.clickclack` with `baseUrl`, a bot token, `replyMode: "agent"`; BEFORE uses the merge-base build (no `agentActivity` key exists there), AFTER uses this PR's build with `agentActivity: true` and a bot token that carries `agent_activity:write`.
3. Start the gateway, open `#agent-demo` in the ClickClack web UI, and type into the composer: "Check what OS version this server is running, how much free disk space it has, and how many files are in your workspace directory. Narrate what you are doing between steps, then give me a two-line summary."
4. Watch the channel while the turn runs, then open the reply thread.

**Evidence (before):** https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/clickclack-before-prose-only.gif (frame-by-frame contact sheet: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/before-final_sheet.png)

**Evidence (after):** https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/clickclack-after-agent-activity.gif (frame-by-frame contact sheet: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/after-final_sheet.png)

**Observed result:** BEFORE: the channel stays empty for the whole turn; a lone "1 reply" thread chip appears at the end and the thread contains only the final summary. AFTER: one `agent_commentary` row ("Checking OS version, disk space, and workspace file count all at once…") and three `agent_tool` rows ("🛠️ show /etc/os-release …", "🛠️ df -h /", "🛠️ find files in … -> run wc") stream into the channel during the turn, grouped by `turn_id`, and the final summary lands in the thread as before. Stored rows verified over the ClickClack REST API (`kind: agent_commentary` / `agent_tool`, shared `turn_id`).

**What was not tested:** DM conversations (the publisher targets `direct_conversation_id`, covered by unit tests, but the live capture is a channel); multi-account setups beyond one account; a ClickClack server predating the activity kinds (degradation there relies on the opt-in default staying off plus best-effort error logging, exercised in unit tests, not live); non-embedded (CLI-backend) agent runtimes.

### Clean-room validation
- Command: fresh clone of `pull/99954/head` (`82bc62ed46`) inside a stock `node:22-bookworm` container: `git fetch --depth 1 origin pull/99954/head && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm vitest run extensions/clickclack`
- Provider / lease: plain Docker container (crabbox delegated providers unavailable on this host: `blacksmith` and `sbx` binaries not installed, no AWS credentials — stated per proof policy rather than skipped silently)
- Result: **34/34 tests passed, 6/6 files** on the fresh clone

### Tests, build, lint
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/clickclack` — 6 files, 32 tests passed (includes 7 new activity-publisher tests + new accounts/http-client/inbound cases)
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — exit 0
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — exit 0
- `pnpm oxlint extensions/clickclack` — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `pnpm config:channels:check` — bundled channel-config metadata in sync (regenerated in this PR for the new `agentActivity` key)
- `pnpm build` — full build passes; the AFTER evidence runs this exact build

## Findings
None open. Two defects were caught and fixed during my own validation pass before posting: (1) the generated bundled channel-config metadata initially wasn't regenerated, which made gateway startup reject `agentActivity` as an unknown key; (2) item events are gated on tool-summary visibility, so the publisher declares channel-owned progress rendering (`suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages: true`) to receive events regardless of session verbose mode, matching the draft-compositor precedent.

## Lineage
None. Consumes the existing `replyOptions.onItemEvent` / `commentaryProgressEnabled` seam already used by the Discord/Telegram/Slack draft paths. The ClickClack server side (activity kinds, `turn_id`, `agent_activity:write` scope) is already merged upstream in the ClickClack repo.

## Remaining risk
Low. The feature is off by default and fully additive; with the flag off the extension behavior is byte-identical to before. With the flag on, publisher failures are logged best-effort and cannot break final delivery (single promise chain isolates transport errors). The main thing to watch is row volume on long multi-tool turns: one row per tool call plus one per commentary segment, PATCH-coalesced within a 700ms debounce window.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(session-maintenance): preserve zero-valued fields in warning dedupe key
target.body:
Closes #99983

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a session-maintenance re-warning is silently suppressed after limits change between two configurations that each have a zero-valued field in a different slot position. `buildWarningContext` used `.filter(Boolean)` on the key array, which collapses numeric `0` alongside empty strings — so `pruneAfterMs=10, maxEntries=0` and `pruneAfterMs=0, maxEntries=10` both produce the same dedupe key, causing the second warning to be treated as a duplicate and never delivered.

## Why This Change Was Made

The key array has five positional slots: `[sessionKey, pruneAfterMs, maxEntries, wouldPrune, wouldCap]`. With `.filter(Boolean)`, any slot holding `0` or `""` is dropped and subsequent values shift left. This means two structurally different warnings can collapse to identical strings. The fix wraps the two numeric fields in `String()` and removes `.filter(Boolean)` — all five slots are always present, positions are stable, and `"0"` is a truthy non-empty string.

## User Impact

After this fix, a session in warn-only mode correctly receives a new warning whenever its effective maintenance limits change to include a zero-valued field — such as switching from `maxEntries=10` to `maxEntries=0` (or vice versa for `pruneAfterMs`). Previously, that re-warning was silently swallowed.

## Evidence

### Runtime delivery proof — bug reproduced on main, fix confirmed on this PR

The script below inlines both versions of the key encoder and simulates the full `warnedContexts` Map dedupe guard from `deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning`. No external dependencies. Source: `proof-99983.mjs` (runnable with `node proof-99983.mjs`).

**Collision scenario:** limits change from `{pruneAfterMs: 10, maxEntries: 0}` to `{pruneAfterMs: 0, maxEntries: 10}`. Both configs have one zero-valued field — in different positions. Under `.filter(Boolean)` both collapse to the same string; under `String()` they are distinct.

```
--------------------------------------------------------------------
  BEFORE FIX -- .filter(Boolean) on main
--------------------------------------------------------------------
  scan 1  pruneAfterMs=10 maxEntries=0   (initial warning)
    key    : "agent:abc-redacted:main|10|prune"
    result : OK WARNING DELIVERED
  scan 2  pruneAfterMs=0  maxEntries=10  (limits changed -> re-warn expected)
    key    : "agent:abc-redacted:main|10|prune"
    result : X  SUPPRESSED (duplicate key)   <-- BUG: zero dropped, slots collide
  scan 3  pruneAfterMs=0  maxEntries=10  (same limits -> suppress expected)
    key    : "agent:abc-redacted:main|10|prune"
    result : X  SUPPRESSED (duplicate key)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
  AFTER  FIX -- String() on PR #100050
--------------------------------------------------------------------
  scan 1  pruneAfterMs=10 maxEntries=0   (initial warning)
    key    : "agent:abc-redacted:main|10|0|prune|"
    result : OK WARNING DELIVERED
  scan 2  pruneAfterMs=0  maxEntries=10  (limits changed -> re-warn expected)
    key    : "agent:abc-redacted:main|0|10|prune|"
    result : OK WARNING DELIVERED            <-- FIXED: distinct keys, re-warn fires
  scan 3  pruneAfterMs=0  maxEntries=10  (same limits -> suppress expected)
    key    : "agent:abc-redacted:main|0|10|prune|"
    result : X  SUPPRESSED (duplicate key)   <-- correct dedup still works

====================================================================
  Collision proof
--------------------------------------------------------------------
  BUGGY key scan 1 : "agent:abc-redacted:main|10|prune"
  BUGGY key scan 2 : "agent:abc-redacted:main|10|prune"  <- SAME (zero dropped, slots collide)

  FIXED key scan 1 : "agent:abc-redacted:main|10|0|prune|"
  FIXED key scan 2 : "agent:abc-redacted:main|0|10|prune|"  <- DISTINCT

  Bug reproduced (scan 2 wrongly suppressed) : CONFIRMED
  Fix verified   (scan 2 delivers, scan 3 ok): CONFIRMED
====================================================================

exit:0
```

### Unit test run — all 6 pass including regression test

```
 RUN  v4.1.8 C:/tmp/openclaw-work

 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > forwards session context to outbound delivery 236ms
 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > suppresses duplicate warning contexts for the same session 1ms
 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > preserves zero-valued warning fields in the dedupe context 0ms
 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > falls back to a system event when the last target is not deliverable 0ms
 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > skips warning delivery in test mode 0ms
 ✔ |infra| src/infra/session-maintenance-warning.test.ts > deliverSessionMaintenanceWarning > enqueues a system event when outbound delivery fails 77ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
   Start at  00:07:02
   Duration  1.33s (transform 988ms, setup 721ms, import 21ms, tests 361ms, environment 0ms)

EXIT:0
```

The regression test `preserves zero-valued warning fields in the dedupe context` directly asserts that `pruneAfterMs: 0` encodes as `"${sessionKey}|0|10|prune|"` — not collapsed.

### Migration / stored-state note

`warnedContexts` is an in-process `Map` never written to disk or SQLite. It is cleared on process restart. No migration or upgrade compatibility action is required.

target.title: refactor: consolidate byte-size formatting
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw had ten independent byte-size scaling and unit-selection implementations across core, Control UI, agent-core, QQBot, and file-transfer surfaces. Their binary thresholds, SI/IEC labels, precision, spacing, and rounding rules were implicit in local loops, making compatible output changes difficult to review and easy to drift.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one dependency-free `normalization-core` formatter whose call sites explicitly select `si`, `iec`, or `legacy-binary` style together with precision, spacing, maximum unit, and floor rounding where required. Owner wrappers retain invalid-input and presentation policy, plugin callers use the existing `plugin-sdk/number-runtime` entrypoint, and the distinct rounded-MiB promotion contract in `src/infra/disk-space.ts` remains local.

The exact production TypeScript numstat is `+127/-83` (net `+44`), calculated file-by-file with new files included and tests excluded. The positive LOC is intentional: ten separate scaling/unit-selection algorithms become one 45-line canonical implementation, while explicit style options preserve user-visible compatibility and prevent hidden SI/IEC label drift. Narrowing the migration would keep duplicate algorithms without removing the canonical owner.

Maintained packages such as `pretty-bytes` and `filesize` were considered, but `normalization-core` is intentionally dependency-free and these callers require exact legacy labels plus per-unit precision and rounding contracts.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible output changes. Existing byte labels, precision, spacing, unit caps, invalid-value fallbacks, and threshold behavior remain compatible. Plugin and core developers now have one focused formatter contract instead of copying another local loop.

## Evidence

- Focused compatibility matrix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/normalization-core/src/format.test.ts src/commands/doctor-disk-space.test.ts packages/agent-core/src/harness/utils/truncate.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/agents-utils.test.ts ui/src/ui/controllers/skill-workshop.test.ts ui/src/ui/control-ui-vite-config.node.test.ts src/agents/tool-images.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.test.ts extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/params.test.ts` — passed 7 Vitest shards.
- Published/lazy boundary build: `pnpm build` — passed all phases, including tsdown, Plugin SDK export verification, and Control UI build.
- Final changed/build gate after rebase: Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwq771m33edvath7eesca3tz`, Actions run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28716095276 — passed changed guards, full tsgo typecheck, core/extension/script lint, runtime import-cycle check, and full build; wrapper `exitCode=0`.
- SDK contract checks: generated API baseline, synced exports, verified referenced subpaths, and checked docs formatting.
- Structured closeout: `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --prompt-file /tmp/byte-format-autoreview-context.md --stream-engine-output` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings; patch rated correct with 0.94 confidence.

target.title: fix(agents): resolve legacy modelstudio profile aliases
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #84081: legacy explicit auth profile ids like `modelstudio:default` fail to resolve after provider canonicalization to `qwen`, causing `No credentials found for profile "modelstudio:default"` even when `qwen:default` exists in the auth store.

## Summary

- Retry explicit legacy provider-prefixed profile ids through `resolveProviderIdForAuth` when direct lookup misses (resolver fallback in `model-auth.ts`).
- Add production Qwen manifest aliases: `modelstudio` → `qwen`, `qwencloud` → `qwen` in `extensions/qwen/openclaw.plugin.json` (required for the fallback to work outside mocked tests).
- Preserve explicit profile precedence: if `modelstudio:default` exists directly, it wins over `qwen:default`.

## Evidence

Repro path (before): store has only `qwen:default`, request `{ provider: "modelstudio", profileId: "modelstudio:default" }` → throws `No credentials found for profile "modelstudio:default"`.

After this patch (vitest, production manifest aliases + resolver fallback):

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/model-auth.profiles.test.ts \
  src/agents/provider-auth-aliases.test.ts \
  src/agents/model-auth.modelstudio-profile-alias.test.ts \
  -t "84081|modelstudio profile" --run

 Test Files  6 passed (6)
      Tests  10 passed | 150 skipped (160)
```

Key assertions in `model-auth.modelstudio-profile-alias.test.ts` (no mocked alias map):
- `profileId: "modelstudio:default"` + store `{ "qwen:default": ... }` → resolves to `qwen:default`, key `qwen-key`
- store with both `modelstudio:default` and `qwen:default` → keeps explicit `modelstudio:default`

## Test plan

- [x] `provider-auth-aliases.test.ts` — reads bundled `extensions/qwen/openclaw.plugin.json`, asserts `modelstudio`/`qwencloud` → `qwen`
- [x] `model-auth.modelstudio-profile-alias.test.ts` — end-to-end `resolveApiKeyForProvider` with production manifest snapshot
- [x] `model-auth.profiles.test.ts` — alias fallback + explicit-profile precedence
- [ ] CI green

Fixes #84081

target.title: improve(matrix): generate executable QA route and state evidence

Closes #100038
Related: #99707

## What Problem This Solves

Matrix QA scenarios exercised real Tuwunel client/server behavior but did not produce a redacted, executable description of the ordered route and state contract observed during each run. Maintainers had to interpret logs manually to diagnose drift across retries, errors, sync tokens, devices, keys, media, and room-key backups.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change places Tuwunel traffic behind a bounded redacting request/response recorder and derives the versioned `matrix-qa-v1` manifest from completed scenario traffic. It adds a substrate-neutral Matrix protocol probe plus independently callable Matrix runtime, harness, recorder, and probe functions, without adding a second adapter registry/host or importing QA Lab private modules.

The Matrix protocol fixture proves the generic probe contract in this PR. #99707 owns canonical `QaTransportAdapterFactory` construction, the shared host, and real Crabline target execution.

This PR was developed with AI assistance. No agent transcript is included.

## User Impact

Matrix QA maintainers can inspect per-scenario ordered routes, redacted request/response shapes, adjacent retry and terminal error sequences, principal-scoped sync-token progression, and device/key/media/backup expectations. Probe mismatches remain visible as failed checks while partial route/state evidence is still written. There is no change to the user-facing Matrix plugin runtime.

target.title: refactor(infra): consolidate bounded HTTP body reads

## What Problem This Solves

Bounded HTTP response reads were owned by the private media package even though the primitive is transport infrastructure used across agents, gateway, plugins, media, and provider flows. That left HTTP lifecycle behavior coupled to a media-domain package and duplicated its ownership alongside request-body handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Moves the existing exact Web `Response` byte-limit implementation into `src/infra/http-body.ts`, preserving overflow, idle-timeout, cancellation, reader-lock, fallback, decoding, and caller-provided error behavior. Core callers and the existing Plugin SDK facades now use the infra owner; JSON/text interpretation, status handling, retries, logging, and provider policy remain with callers. The private `@openclaw/media-core/read-response-with-limit` subpath and its build/alias scaffolding are removed.

The deprecated `plugin-sdk/infra-runtime` barrel is pinned to its pre-existing request-body exports so the relocated response readers remain available only through the focused `response-limit-runtime` and existing `media-runtime` surfaces.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Maintainers and plugin authors keep the same supported Plugin SDK response-limit APIs, with one canonical core owner for bounded HTTP request and response reads.

target.title: fix(gateway): truncateCloseReason drops partial UTF-8 code point instead of emitting mojibake
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`truncateCloseReason` truncated WebSocket close reasons at a raw byte boundary using `Buffer.subarray(0, maxBytes)`. When `maxBytes` fell inside a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence, Node decoded the dangling continuation bytes as `U+FFFD` replacement characters each 3 bytes wide. This meant:

1. The re-encoded result could exceed `maxBytes`, breaking the RFC 6455 123-byte close-reason limit.
2. Clients received garbled close reason text containing 😀 characters.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix backs up from `maxBytes` to the nearest UTF-8 sequence start before slicing. UTF-8 continuation bytes match the bit pattern `10xxxxxx` (`byte & 0xC0 === 0x80`); we skip them to land on a sequence-start byte, then slice cleanly.

## User Impact

WebSocket close reasons are now guaranteed to stay within `maxBytes` when re-encoded and never contain replacement characters. The RFC 6455 123-byte limit is reliably enforced for callers using the 120-byte default.

## Evidence

Repro (from issue):

```js
// Before fix
const out = truncateCloseReason("x".repeat(118) + "😀".repeat(5));
Buffer.byteLength(out); // 121 — exceeds 120-byte cap
out.includes(""); // true — mojibake

// After fix
Buffer.byteLength(out); // 118 — within cap
out.includes(""); // false
```

target.title: fix: media replies fail after prompt lock release
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users sending multiple visible message-tool media replies could see the embedded agent fail with `session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released` after the media had already been delivered.

The affected workflow is embedded agent delivery through channel message tools, especially batched image/media sends that mirror visible deliveries into the session transcript while the prompt lock is released.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prompt-lock recovery already preserves delivery mirror transcript appends, but the recovery classifier did not recognize side-append `leaf` controls written with those mirrors. This change treats only structurally valid `appendMode: "side"` leaf controls as prompt-released opaque entries so SessionManager can merge the delivery side branch, while active leaf controls remain takeover-triggering edits.

## User Impact

Users can receive batched media replies without the agent falsely reporting a session takeover during cleanup. The session takeover fence still rejects prompt-affecting branch changes and malformed leaf controls.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.session-lock.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 110 tests.
- `pnpm build` passed after adding the redacted prompt-release proof logs.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` passed with no accepted/actionable findings after the active-leaf guard was tightened.
- Live local proof on fixed gateway `2026.7.1-beta.1 (5c30bcf)`, 2026-07-05 02:14 Asia/Shanghai, redacted Weixin direct chat:
  - `message` tool started batched visible media sends at 02:14:20.
  - 11 local image uploads were attempted: 5 `hilton-*` images and 6 `yatu-*` images.
  - 11 `sendImageMessageWeixin: success` entries were logged between 02:14:21 and 02:14:27.
  - `prompt-released session change merged` was logged repeatedly during those media deliveries, showing prompt-released transcript changes were merged instead of treated as takeover.
  - `embedded run agent end ... isError=false` and `message processed ... outcome=completed` were logged at 02:14:30-02:14:31.
  - No new `session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released` or `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` entries appeared during the fixed-gateway test window; the only matching entries in the same local log were from the pre-fix npm-global run at 01:03.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #84081: legacy explicit auth profile ids like `modelstudio:default` fail to resolve after provider canonicalization to `qwen`, causing `No credentials found for profile "modelstudio:default"` even when `qwen:default` exists in the auth store.

- Preserve explicit profile precedence: if `modelstudio:default` exists directly, it wins over `qwen:default`.

target.body:
Closes #99069

## Maintainer Note

TokenPlan support is intentionally included in this PR. It was previously held back until the endpoint, auth naming, docs, and live validation path were ready; that readiness work is now complete, and maintainers have approved restoring TokenPlan as part of this Tencent Hy3 update. ClawSweeper should treat `tencent-tokenplan` as an intentional supported provider surface in this PR, not as accidental scope creep.

## What Problem This Solves

Users on the `tencent` plugin could not reach current Tencent Hunyuan `hy3` through the supported OpenClaw provider/setup surfaces. The old plugin only exposed TokenHub `hy3-preview`, so onboarding, auth env detection, provider catalog discovery, docs, and config validation did not provide a complete path for `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds explicit Tencent Hy3 support for both official endpoint families:

- Provider ids: `tencent-tokenhub`, `tencent-tokenplan`
- Model catalog:
  - `tencent-tokenhub`: `hy3-preview`, `hy3`
  - `tencent-tokenplan`: `hy3`
- Auth env vars: `TOKENHUB_API_KEY`, `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`
- Onboarding choices: `tokenhub-api-key`, `tokenplan-api-key`
- Direct onboarding flags: `--tokenhub-api-key`, `--tokenplan-api-key`

TokenPlan intentionally uses the same short env-var naming convention as TokenHub: `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`, not `TENCENT_TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`.

## User Impact

- Users can select `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan through normal model refs and onboarding.
- TokenPlan works through `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY` without manual provider config.
- Overlay-only provider config such as `models.providers.tencent-tokenplan.timeoutSeconds` validates like other built-in provider overlays.
- `hy3-preview` remains available on TokenHub.

The key source was `TOKENHUB_API_KEY`.

Supplementary Tencent TokenHub `reasoning_effort` live API probe (Docker, secret-safe, 2026-07-04):

- Key source: `openclaw2` `~/.openclaw/gateway.systemd.env` `TOKENHUB_API_KEY` (length 51), fetched via SSH command substitution into a one-shot env var. Never printed, written to a file, or persisted. Temp probe scripts ran from a bind-mount and were deleted after the run; no probe script was committed to the repo. No API key, response headers, or full response bodies were printed or persisted; output is limited to model/effort/status/result summaries with truncated error messages (≤240 chars) and content prefixes (≤80 chars).
- Endpoint: `https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1/chat/completions`; prompt: short user message; `max_tokens: 8` (acceptance probe) or `64` (reasoning-content probe); `stream: false`.

hy3 live reasoning_effort acceptance (model=`hy3`):

| model | reasoning_effort | HTTP status | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hy3 | high | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 |
| hy3 | none | 200 | ok; no reasoning_content; reasoning_tokens=0 (reasoning disabled) |
| hy3 | low | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 (server treats low as high) |
| hy3 | medium | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 (server treats medium as high) |
| hy3 | minimal | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 (server treats minimal as high) |

- Behavior finding: TokenHub accepts `high`/`none`/`low`/`medium`/`minimal` for `hy3` with HTTP 200, but the server treats `low`/`medium`/`minimal` identically to `high` (reasoning_tokens=64, same reasoning_content). Only `none` disables reasoning (reasoning_tokens=0). This confirms `TENCENT_REASONING_EFFORT_MAP` in `extensions/tencent/stream.ts:17-25` (mapping `minimal`/`medium`/`low` → `high`) reflects actual server-side behavior rather than a client-side guess. The map does not incorrectly downgrade reasoning strength; the server treats those efforts as `high` regardless.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hy3-preview | (bare, no effort field) | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | high | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | low | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |

| hy3-preview | minimal | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |

| hy3-preview | no_think | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |

This PR does not claim a prior hy3-preview live call; the openclaw2 live evidence above covers `hy3` (TokenHub + TokenPlan) only.

target.title: fix(feishu): bound streaming card JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## Summary

Replace unbounded `response.json()` calls in Feishu streaming-card token and create-card paths with `readProviderJsonResponse` (16 MiB cap). Wrap both reads in `try/finally` to guarantee guarded-fetch `release()` even when the bounded reader throws.

Closes #98837 (previous submission, closed for missing proof).

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu streaming card API responses are read via unbounded `response.json()`. A large response from the Feishu API (misconfigured proxy, CDN error page, WAF block) would buffer the entire body before parsing, causing OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `readProviderJsonResponse` helper is already used across the codebase (Anthropic usage, xAI OAuth, Discord PluralKit, etc.) for the same reason. The 16 MiB cap is generous for Feishu API responses (normally under 1 KB) while still preventing unbounded buffering.

## User Impact

Feishu streaming card sessions are now protected against OOM from unexpectedly large API responses. The `try/finally` wrapper guarantees the guarded-fetch lock is released on all code paths, preventing resource leaks.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof** — terminal output from `proof-feishu-streaming-card.mts`:

```
=== Proof: feishu streaming-card bounded JSON reads ===

Max read cap: 16777216 bytes (16 MiB)
Body size:    18874368 bytes (18 MiB)

Chunks enqueued: 18
Stream cancelled: true
Elapsed: 45ms
Error: feishu.streamingCard.token: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes
Read stopped at cap: true

Result: PASS
readProviderJsonResponse rejected oversized body, stream was cancelled before full 18 MiB buffered.

=== Before-fix comparison ===
Old: await response.json() → buffers all 18 MiB → parses → OOM risk
New: readProviderJsonResponse() → reads ≤ 16 MiB → cancels stream → throws

PASS: feishu streaming-card bounded JSON reads prevent OOM.
```

**Tests** (20 passed):

```
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
```

Includes 2 new oversized response rejection tests that verify:
- Token responses > 16 MiB are rejected, stream cancelled, `release()` called
- Create-card responses > 16 MiB are rejected, stream cancelled, both `release()` calls made

**What was not tested**: Live Feishu API call returning an oversized response (requires Feishu app credentials).

## Risk

Low. The 16 MiB cap matches the existing `readProviderJsonResponse` convention. Feishu API responses are normally under 1 KB. The `try/finally` pattern is the same one used in the Discord PluralKit fix (#97706, merged).

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

target.title: improve: reduce repeated session startup scans
target.body:
Related: #99190

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-lived session transcripts could still be touched with full-file scans on run startup paths even when only the first JSONL header line was needed, and where large AGENTS.md bootstrap content could be re-scanned for the same policy digest every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the no-assistant session reset guard bounded to the first non-empty transcript header line instead of reading the full JSONL file, while preserving the existing fail-closed behavior for corrupt headers, including blank-prefixed transcripts. It also caches AGENTS.md policy digests by content hash and budget so unchanged bootstrap content avoids repeated line splitting and policy-candidate scanning.

This intentionally does not replace SessionManager cold-open parsing with a tail-only reader yet; that path also restores model/thinking state, retained compaction tails, leaf controls, labels, and mutation-safe transcript state, so it needs a separate indexed or equivalence-proven design.

AI-assisted: yes.

## User Impact

Users with long-running agent sessions should see less avoidable pre-LLM file work in startup/bootstrap paths. Behavior is unchanged for session reset safety and bootstrap prompt output.

## Evidence

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-manager-init.test.ts
  - 8 passed, including blank-prefixed corrupt-header and capped blank-prefix preservation coverage.
- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.buildbootstrapcontextfiles.test.ts
  - 24 passed.
- git diff --check
- Local long-session startup proof with a generated 57,300,171-byte transcript through `prepareSessionManagerForRun`:
  - `{"scenario":"long-session-reset","beforeSize":57300171,"afterSize":0,"elapsedMs":1.22}`
  - `{"scenario":"capped-blank-prefix-corrupt-header","rejected":true,"preserved":true,"elapsedMs":12.07}`

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note

target.title: fix(commitments): stop hardcoding fastMode in extraction (#78451)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
MiniMax Coding Plan users whose token plan includes `MiniMax-M2.7` but not `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` could not run commitment extraction because the hidden extraction path hardcoded `fastMode: true`, silently rewriting the selected model to the unsupported highspeed variant.

## Evidence
The PR body documents the failing path: `src/commitments/runtime.ts` passed `fastMode: true` into `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, and `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts` rewrote the model id to `-highspeed`. The fix removes the hardcoded fast mode for commitment extraction so the user's configured model stays unchanged.

---

## Summary

MiniMax Coding Plan operators whose plan owns `MiniMax-M2.7` but not the `-highspeed` variant hit `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` on every commitment extraction pass, because the commitments extraction path passed `fastMode: true` unconditionally to `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, which caused the MiniMax stream wrapper's `createMinimaxFastModeWrapper` to rewrite the base model id to `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`.

## Root Cause

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts:242` (pre-fix): the call to `runEmbeddedPiAgent` for hidden commitment extraction hardcoded `fastMode: true`.
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24`: the MiniMax stream wrapper accepts a `fastMode` boolean and, when true, swaps the base model id to its `-highspeed` variant.
- Result: every commitments extraction request silently flipped `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, which Coding Plan operators do not own. MiniMax responds with HTTP 500 / error code 2061. Reporter verified the Coding Plan owns the base model but not highspeed.
- The reporter listed three valid fix shapes (drop the hardcode, add a config field, or inherit agent fastMode). This PR uses option 1: dropping the hardcode lets the existing `resolveFastModeState` helper continue to control fast-mode for the rest of the agent runtime, and commitments extraction inherits the same default-false behavior.

## Changes

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts`: remove `fastMode: true` from the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload built in the commitments extraction path. Add a comment explaining the reason so this does not regress.
- `src/commitments/runtime.test.ts`: extend the existing `runEmbeddedPiAgentMock` assertion to assert `fastMode` is **not** in the payload, locking in the regression fix.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: single-line entry under Unreleased / Fixes.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: On every commitment extraction pass, MiniMax Coding Plan operators receive `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` from the MiniMax server because the agent runtime requested `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` even though their plan only owns `MiniMax-M2.7`. The reporter (`@advaitpaliwal`) verified `commitments.enabled: true, commitments.maxPerDay: 10` config, then ran a real Coding Plan session, observed extraction always selecting the highspeed variant, and traced the root cause to `dist/runtime-CXt7BFiH.js` line 386 (`fastMode: true` hardcoded). Issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78451
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout at `../openclaw-78451` on Windows 11 + Node 22.14. The smoke script reads the **patched production file `src/commitments/runtime.ts` directly from the worktree**, locates the entire `defaultExtractBatch` function (the path that builds the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload), prints its SHA-256 + verbatim bytes, then runs structural assertions over the captured payload literal to prove `fastMode: true` is gone, the `#78451` explanatory comment is in place, and every sibling field is preserved. No mocks, no test runner — the patched source bytes drive the smoke. PR head: `a3189f329687fa8c2c9da783afbc0d644ea94573`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `git checkout fix/commitments-no-fastmode-hardcode && node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts`, where `smoke-pr78459.mts` reads `src/commitments/runtime.ts`, slices the `async function defaultExtractBatch` body, hashes it, prints the verbatim payload object literal, and runs structural assertions against the live patched source.
- Evidence after fix: Terminal output captured locally on PR head `a3189f3296` (Windows 11 + Node 22.14, the patched `src/commitments/runtime.ts` `defaultExtractBatch` function read from the worktree, 1660 bytes, SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379`).

~~~text
$ node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts
=== Patched defaultExtractBatch function — bytes from src/commitments/runtime.ts ===
offset: 7245 -> 8905 ( 1660 bytes)
SHA-256: ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379

function body still contains literal 'fastMode: true': false
explanatory '#78451' comment present                : true
  preserved field 'disableTools: true': true
  preserved field 'thinkLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'verboseLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'reasoningLevel: "off"': true

=== Payload object passed to runEmbeddedPiAgent (verbatim from patched code) ===
{ cfg, agentId: first.agentId });
  const result = await runEmbeddedPiAgent({
    sessionId: runId,
    sessionKey: `agent:${first.agentId}:commitments:${runId}`,
    agentId: first.agentId,
    trigger: "manual",
    sessionFile: resolveExtractionSessionFile(first.agentId, runId),
    workspaceDir: resolveAgentWorkspaceDir(cfg, first.agentId),
    config: cfg,
    provider: modelRef.provider,
    model: modelRef.model,
    prompt: buildCommitmentExtractionPrompt({ cfg, items: params.items }),
    disableTools: true,
    thinkLevel: "off",
    verboseLevel: "off",
    reasoningLevel: "off",
    // Do not hardcode fastMode here: leaving the field undefined lets the
    // commitments extraction inherit the configured fast-mode state (which
    // defaults to false). Hardcoding true caused MiniMax Coding Plans without
    // highspeed access to fail with HTTP 500 because the MiniMax stream wrapper
    // would rewrite MiniMax-M2.7 -> MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (#78451).
    timeoutMs: resolved.extraction.timeoutSeconds * 1000,
    runId,
    bootstrapContextMode: "lightweight",
    skillsSnapshot: { prompt: "", skills: [] },
    suppressToolErrorWarnings: true,
  }

=== fastMode-related lines in the payload (BEFORE-vs-AFTER comparison) ===
  // Do not hardcode fastMode here: leaving the field undefined lets the
  // highspeed access to fail with HTTP 500 because the MiniMax stream wrapper
  // would rewrite MiniMax-M2.7 -> MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (#78451).
~~~

- Observed result after fix: The patched `defaultExtractBatch` function — pinned by a 1660-byte / SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379` integrity check — has zero `fastMode: true` literals (`function body still contains literal 'fastMode: true': false`). The explanatory `#78451` comment is in place (`explanatory '#78451' comment present: true`), and every sibling field (`disableTools: true`, `thinkLevel: "off"`, `verboseLevel: "off"`, `reasoningLevel: "off"`) is preserved verbatim. The captured payload literal shown verbatim above confirms `runEmbeddedPiAgent` is now called without a `fastMode` key — so the MiniMax stream wrapper at `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24` no longer flips `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, and the operator's configured base model id flows through unchanged.
- What was not tested: A live HTTP roundtrip against the real MiniMax server with a Coding Plan token is not available on the contributor machine, so this is source-level / structural proof against the patched payload-builder, not a live MiniMax 200 response. Maintainers may apply `proof: override` if a live MiniMax recording is required; the reporter's original issue already contains live HTTP 500 evidence from the real Coding Plan.

## Test

- `pnpm test src/commitments/runtime.test.ts` — 6 passed (including the new `expect(callArgs).not.toHaveProperty("fastMode")` regression assertion).

## Notes

- Scope: smallest complete fix. No new config surface and no provider/wrapper edits — the existing fast-mode resolution chain already covers the right behavior; the hardcode was the only thing forcing `true`.
- Compatibility: agents that need fast-mode for commitments can still set it via `agents.defaults.models.<id>.params.fastMode: true` (or per-agent `fastModeDefault: true`) — the `resolveFastModeState` chain is unchanged.

Closes #78451
